lines.text: Honey, wait. We only did it once. It didn't mean anything to me.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah, right. Sure!

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Really, Rachel, I was thinking of you the whole time. Look, I'm sorry,
all right. I never meant for you to find out!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, please, you wanted to get caught. (Waves the receipt)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: That is not true!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, so you just sort of happened to leave it in here?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Did it ever occur to you that I might just be that stupid?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Ok, Monica. I just have to know one thing. Did you go with her to Bloomingdale's?
(Monica looks away.) Oh! Ok, ok, ok, I just really, uh, I just really need to not be with
you right now. (Exits.)
Commercial Break
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's, Ben is playing in his crib while Chandler and Ross are
leaning against the rim and are completely asleep.]

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (on the phone) Hi, who's this? (Listens) Hi, Joanne. Is Rachel working?
It's Monica. (Listens) Yes, I know I did a horrible thing. (Listens) Joanne, it's not as
simple as all that, ok? (Listens) No, I don't care what Steve thinks. (Listens) Hi, Steve.
(There's a knock on the door which is answered by Phoebe.)

lines.speaker: Carol and Susan
lines.text: Hey! (This wakes Chandler and Ross up)

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: How did we do?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh, I tasted Ben's milk, and Ross freaked out.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I did not freak out.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: Why'd you freak out?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Because it's breast milk. It's gross.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: My breast milk is gross?

lines.speaker: Susan
lines.text: This should be fun.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No, no, Carol. There's nothing wrong with it. I just, I just don't think
breast milk is for adults.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Of course the packaging does appeal to grown-ups and kids alike.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: Ross, you're being silly. I've tried it, it's no big deal. Just taste it.
(Holding out a bottle.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (jumping away) That would be no.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Come on. It doesn't taste bad.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Yeah, it's kinda sweet, sorta like, uh...

lines.speaker: Susan
lines.text: Cantaloupe juice.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (staring at Susan) You've tasted it? You've tasted it.

lines.speaker: Susan
lines.text: Uh huh.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, you've tasted it.

lines.speaker: Susan
lines.text: You can keep saying it, but it won't stop being true.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (he rolls up his sleeve) Gimme the bottle. (Joey hands him the bottle and
Ross squirts some on his arm.) Gimme the towel. (Joey gives him the towel and he wipes it
off.)
[Scene: Chandler and Joey's, Chandler is wiping down the peninsula counter as Joey
enters dressed like a cowboy.]

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Howdy.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (sitting on the otherside of the counter from Chandler) Gimme a box a
juice. Well, they switched me over to Hombre.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well, maybe it's because of the way you're dressed.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Or maybe it's because this guy's doing so good they wanna put more people
on it. (Chandler pours some juice in a glass.) You should see this guy, Chandler, he goes
through two bottles a day.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (slides the juice across the counter which Joey catches) What do you
care? You're an actor. This is your day job. This isn't supposed to mean anything to you.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: I know, but, I was the best, you know? I liked being the best. (He downs
the glass of juice in one swig.) I don't know. Maybe I should just get outta the game.
They need guys up in housewares to serve cheese.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (pours more and slides the refill to Joey) All right, say you do that.
You know sooner or later somebody's gonna come along that slices a better cheddar. And
then where're you gonna run?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Yeah I guess you're right.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: You're damn right I'm right. I say you show this guy what you're made
of. I say you stand your ground. I say you show him that you are the baddest hombre west
of the lingerie.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: I'm gonna do it. (He downs the juice in one swig again.)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: All right. Now go see Miss Kitty and she'll fix you up with a nice
hooker.

scenes.location: Outside Central Perk, Rachel is cleaning up and Monica is pleading with her.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I don't know what else to say.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Well that works out good, because I'm not listening.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I feel terrible, I really do.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, I'm sorry, did my back hurt your knife?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Rachel, (they go back inside) say that I'm friends with her, we spend
some time together. Is that so terrible?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: It's that terrible?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yes. Monica, you don't get it. It's bad enough that she's stolen the guy
who might actually be the person that I am supposed to be with, but now, she's actually
(starting to cry), but now she's actually stealing you.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Me? What are you talking about? Nobody could steal me from you. I mean,
just because I'm friends with her doesn't make me any less friends with you. I mean,
(starting to cry) you're my...We're, we're...Oh, I love you.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I love you too. (They hug.)

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: You guys, um I know that this really doesn't have anything to do with
me, but um I love you guys too. (Joins in on the hug.) Oh, I really needed that. (Goes and
sits down.)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Look, I know that you're in a place right now where you really need to
hate Julie's guts, but she didn't do anything wrong. I mean, she was just a girl who met a
guy, and now they go out. I really think that if you gave her a chance, you'd like her.
Would you just give that a chance, for me?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (crying) I'd do anything for you, you know that.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (crying) I'd do anything for you. (They hug again.)

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Wait, wait, wait, wait! (Runs over and joins in on the hug again.)
[Scene: The Department Store, Joey and the Hombre man are facing off in Joey's
section.]

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Mornin'. (The Hombre man ignores him) I said, mornin'.

lines.speaker: Hombre Man
lines.text: I heard ya.

lines.speaker: Store Guy
lines.text: All right, everybody, I'm openin' the doors. You boys ready?

lines.speaker: Hombre Man
lines.text: Ready.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Yeah, I'm ready.
(An old West style showdown starts with Joey and the Hombre Man staring each other down
as the store guy slowly lets in the first customer while Joey and the Hombre Man get ready
to draw. In slow motion they spot the customer, eye each other, draw, and as the
customer walks into the middle Joey's bottle misfires but the Hombre Man spays it into the
customer's eyes.)

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: You idiot, you stupid cowboy, you blinded me, I'm suing!

lines.speaker: Store Guy
lines.text: Oh my god, Todd! What the hell did you do?

lines.speaker: Hombre Man
lines.text: I'm sorry. I am such a doofus. I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry.

lines.speaker: Annabelle
lines.text: (seeing the end result) My god, what happened?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: These new kids, they never last. Sooner or later, they all...stop lastin'.
Listen, uh, what do you say I buy you that cup of coffee now?

lines.speaker: Annabelle
lines.text: Sure.
(They walk off into the sunset, at least a picture of one.)

scenes.location: Central Perk, Julie and Rachel are sitting on the couch.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: So.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: So. I just thought the two of us should hang out for a bit. I mean, you
know, we've never really talked. I guess you'd know that, being one of the two of us,
though, right?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I know, I probably shouldn't even tell you this, but I'm pretty much
totally intimidated by you.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Really? Me?

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Yes. Oh my god, are you kidding? Ross is so crazy about you, and I really
wanted you to like me, and, it's probably me being totally paranoid, but I kinda got the
feeling that maybe you don't.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Well, you're not totally paranoid.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Oy.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Um, ok, uh, oh god, um, when you and uh Ross first started going out, it
was really hard for me, um, for many reasons, which I'm not gonna bore you with now, but
um, I just, I see how happy he is, you know, and how good you guys are together, and um,
Monica's always saying how nice you are, and god I hate it when she's right.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Thanks. Hey, listen, would you like to go to a movie sometime or
something?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah, that'd be great. I'd love it.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: I'd love it too. Shoot, I gotta go. So, I'll talk to you later.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: All right, Julie.

lines.speaker: Julie
lines.text: Bye. (Gets up.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Bye. (After Julie exits.) What a manipulative bitch.

title: The One Where Heckles Dies

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: So how was Joan?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I broke up with her.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: They were huge. When she sneezed, bats flew out of them.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Come on, they were not that huge.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I'm tellin' you, she leaned back, I could see her brain.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: How many perfectly fine women are you gonna reject over the most superficial
insignificant things?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hold it hold it. I gotta side with Chandler on this one. When I first moved to
the city, I went out a couple of times with this girl, really hot, great kisser, but she
had the biggest Adam's apple. It made me nuts.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You or me?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I got it. Uh, Joey, women don't have Adam's apples.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You guys are messin' with me, right?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: That was a good one. For a second there, I was like, "whoa."

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: You name one woman that you broke up with for a real reason.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Maureen Rosilla.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Not hating Yanni is not a real reason.
(knock)

lines.text: Hello, Mr. Heckles.

lines.speaker: MR. HECKLES
lines.text: You're doing it again.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: We're not doing anything.

lines.speaker: MR. HECKLES
lines.text: You're stomping. It's disturbing my birds.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: You don't have birds.

lines.speaker: MR. HECKLES
lines.text: I could have birds.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Ok, Mr. Heckles, we'll try to keep it down.

lines.speaker: MR. HECKLES
lines.text: Thank you. I'm going to rejoin my dinner party.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: All right, bye-bye.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Ok, Janice. Janice. You gotta give me Janice. That wasn't about being picky.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: We'll give you Janice.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I miss Janice though. "Hello, Chandler Bing."

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: "Oh, my, god."

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: "Oh, Chandler, now, now, that's it. There, faster!"

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Stop with the broom, we're not making noise.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: We won. We won!

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Mr. Heckles.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: How did this happen?

lines.speaker: MR. TREEGER
lines.text: He musta been sweepin'. They found a broom in his hand.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: That's terrible.

lines.speaker: MR. TREEGER
lines.text: I know. I was sweepin' yesterday. It coulda been me.ROSS: Sure, sweepin'.
You never know.

lines.speaker: MR. TREEGER
lines.text: You never know.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok, it's very faint, but I can still sense him in the building. Go into the
light, Mr. Heckles!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Ok, Phoebe.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I'm sorry, but sometimes they need help. That's fine. Go ahead and scoff. You
know, there're a lot of things that I don't believe in, but that doesn't mean they're not
true.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Such as?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Like crop circles, or the Bermuda triangle, or evolution?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa. What, you don't, uh, you don't believe in evolution?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Nah. Not really.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You don't believe in evolution?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I don't know, it's just, you know...monkeys, Darwin, you know, it's a, it's a
nice story, I just think it's a little too easy.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Too easy? Too...The process of every living thing on this planet evolving over
millions of years from single-celled organisms, too easy?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Yeah, I just don't buy it.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Uh, excuse me. Evolution is not for you to buy, Phoebe. Evolution is scientific
fact, like, like, like the air we breathe, like gravity.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok, don't get me started on gravity.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You uh, you don't believe in gravity?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Well, it's not so much that you know, like I don't believe in it, you know,
it's just...I don't know, lately I get the feeling that I'm not so much being pulled down
as I am being pushed.
(knock)

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Uh-Oh. It's Isaac Newton, and he's pissed.

lines.speaker: MR. TREEGER
lines.text: There she is. And over there, that's the other one. This is Mr. Buddy
Boyle, Mr. Heckles' attorney. He'd like to talk to you.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: What can we do for you?

lines.speaker: MR. BOYLE
lines.text: All right, kids. Here's the deal. According to my client's will, he wants to
leave all his earthly possessions to "the noisy girls in the apartment above
mine".

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Well, what about his family?

lines.speaker: MR. BOYLE
lines.text: He didn't have any.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok, so let's talk money.

lines.speaker: MR. BOYLE
lines.text: All right, there was none. Let's talk signing. You be noisy girl number one,
you be noisy girl number two.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: I can't believe that this whole time we thought he hated us. I mean, isn't it
amazing how much you can touch someone's life, without even knowing it?...Would you look
at this dump? He hated us. This is his final revenge!

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Have you ever seen so much crap?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Actually, I think this apartment sullies the good name of crap

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Check this out. Can I have this?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: How can you not believe in evolution?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Just don't. Look at this funky shirt!

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Pheebs, I have studied evolution my entire adult life. Ok, I can tell you, we
have collected fossils from all over the world that actually show the evolution of
different species, ok? You can literally see them evolving through time.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Really? You can actually see it?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You bet. In the U.S., China, Africa, all over.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: See, I didn't know that.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Well, there you go.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Huh. So now, the real question is, who put those fossils there, and why?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Hey, look at this. "My Big Book of Grievances."

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, there's me! April 17th. Excessive noise. Italian guy comes homes with a
date. Hey Chandler, look, you're in here too.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: April 18th, excessive noise. Italian guy's gay roommate comes home with the
dry-cleaning. Well that's excellent.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Monica, Monica, look at this lamp. Is this tacky or what? We have to have this.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Rache, I think we have enough regular lamps.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What? Come on, it's not like I'm asking for this girly clock or anything,
which, by the way, I also think is very cool.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: It doesn't go with any of my stuff.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Well, what about my stuff?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: You don't have any stuff.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: You still think of it as your apartment, don't you?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Yes you do. You think of it as your apartment, and I'm just somebody who rents
a room.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Mmmmm.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok, while you "mmm" on it for awhile, I'm gonna go find a place for
my new lamp.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ok, Pheebs. See how I'm making these little toys move? Opposable thumbs. Without
evolution, how do you explain opposable thumbs?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Maybe the overlords needed them to steer their spacecrafts.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Please tell me you're joking.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Look, can't we just say that you believe in something, and I don't.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, no, Pheebs, we can't, ok, because--

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: What is this obsessive need you have to make everyone agree with you? No,
what's that all about? I think, I think maybe it's time you put Ross under the microscope.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Is there blood coming out of my ears?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Check it out, check it out. Heckles' high school yearbook.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Wow, he looks so normal.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: He's even kind of cute.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: "Heckles, you crack me up in science class. You're the funniest kid in
school.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Funniest? Heckles?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: That's what it says.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Wow, Heckles was voted class clown, and so was I. He was right. Would you
listen to that?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I'd call that excessive.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Whoa!

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Heckles played clarinet in band, and I played clarinet. And he was in the
scale modeler's club, and I was, well, there was no club, but I sure thought they were
cool.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: So, you were both dorks. Big deal.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I just think it's weird, you know? Heckles and me, Heckles, and me, me and
Heckles...Would you knock it off?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Have you been here all night?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Look at this. Pictures of all the women that Heckles went out with. Look what
he wrote on them. Vivian, too tall. Madge, big gums. Too loud, too smart, makes noise when
she eats. This is, this is me. This is what I do. I'm gonna end up alone, just like he
did.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Chandler, Heckles was a nut case.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Our trains are on the same track, ok? Yeah, sure, I'm coming up 30 years
behind him, but the stops are all the same. Bitter Town. Aloneville. Hermit Junction.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: All right, you know what we gotta do? We gotta get you outta here. Come on, I'll
buy you breakfast, let's go.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: What if I never find someone? Or worse, what if I've found her, but I dumped
her because she pronounced it "supposably"?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Chandler, come on, you're gonna find somebody.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: How do you know that? How?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: I don't know, I'm just tryin' to help you out.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You'll see, you guys are all gonna go off and get married, and I'm gonna end
up alone. Will you promise me something? When you're married, will you invite me over for
holidays?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know what we're gonna be doin'. I mean, what if we're
at her folks' place?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah, I understand.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You can come over and watch the Super Bowl. Every year, all right?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You know what? I'm not gonna end up like this. I'll see you man.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Supposably. Supposably. Did they go to the zoo? Supposably.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: (on phone) Hi, it's me.

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: Oh, my, god.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Janice? You called Janice?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yes, Janice. Why is that so difficult for you to comprehend?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You remember Janice, right?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yes. She was smart, she was pretty, and she honestly cared about me. Janice
is my last chance to have somebody.

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: Helloo!!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Oh, my, god!

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Geez, look how fat she got.

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: Hey, it's everybody.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Janice, you're--

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: Yes, I am.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Is it--?

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: Is it yours? Ha! You wish, Chandler Bing. You are looking at a married lady
now.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Congratulations.

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: Oh, sweetie, I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You couldn't have told me about this on the phone?

lines.speaker: JANICE
lines.text: And what? Missed the expression on your face? Janice likes to have her fun.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Hey, Rache. You know what we haven't played in a while?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Hide the Lamp.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Monica, let it go.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Did you know I was allergic to shellfish?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Well, then, you'll just have to eat the other lamps.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Uh-oh. It's Scary Scientist Man.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ok, Phoebe, this is it. In this briefcase I carry actual scientific facts. A
briefcase of facts, if you will. Some of these fossils are over 200 million years old.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok, look, before you even start, I'm not denying evolution, ok, I'm just saying
that it's one of the possibilities.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: It's the only possibility, Phoebe.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok, Ross, could you just open your mind like this much, ok? Wasn't there a time
when the brightest minds in the world believed that the world was flat? And, up until like
what, 50 years ago, you all thought the atom was the smallest thing, until you split it
open, and this like, whole mess of crap came out. Now, are you telling me that you are so

lines.text: You'd think, wouldn't you? Miss?

lines.text: Ok, I will have the uh, (whispers) side salad.

lines.speaker: WAITER
lines.text: (whispers) And what will that be on the side of?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Uh, I don't know. Why don't you put it right here next to my water?

lines.text: And for you?

lines.text: Um, I'm gonna have a cup of the cucumber soup, and, um, take care.

lines.text: Oh, thank you!

lines.text: No, huh uh, no way, I'm sorry, not gonna happen.

lines.text: Whoa, whoa, prom night flashback.

lines.text: Ok.

lines.text: We can talk about that.

lines.text: No, the thing was, we were gonna go see Hootie and the Blowfish.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: All of us.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Together.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Not at the concert.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Thanks.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: I don't know, Chandler. Let's take a look.

lines.text: Oh, it's like a skit.

lines.text: Why, it's dinner for six. 5 steaks, and an eggplant for Phoebe.

lines.text: Whoo!

lines.text: Come on.

lines.text: Me neither.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Me too.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Guys, we bought the tickets.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh, well, then you'll have extra seats, you know, for all your tiaras and
stuff.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Why did you look at me when you said that?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Well, I guess now we can't go.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What? Come on, you do what you want to do. Do we always have to do everything
together?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: You know what? You're right.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: All right. We're gonna go. It's not for another six hours. We're gonna go then.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Chandler!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Geez! Are you ready?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah. Just let me grab my jacket and tell you I had sex today.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Whoa! You had sex today?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Wow, it sounds even cooler when somebody else says it. I was awesome, ok? She
was biting her lip to stop from screaming.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Now I know it's been awhile, but I took it as a good sign.
(phone rings)

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Still doing the screening thing?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I had sex today. I never have to answer that phone again.

lines.speaker: MACHINE
lines.text: Here comes the beep, you know what to do.

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Hey, Bob, it's Jade. Listen, I just wanted to tell you that I was really hurt
when you didn't show up the other day, and just so you know, I ended up meeting a guy.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Bob here.

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Oh, hi.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: So, uh, you met someone, huh?

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Yes, yes, I did. In fact, I had sex with him 2 hours ago.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: So, uh, how was he?

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Eh.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Eh?

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Oh, Bob, he was nothing compared to you. I had to bite my lip to keep from
screaming your name.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Well, that makes me feel so good.

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: It was just so awkward and bumpy.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: (silently mouthing) Bumpy?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Well, maybe he had some kind of uh, new, cool style, that you're not familiar
with. And uh maybe you have to get used to it.

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Well there really wasn't much time to get used to it, you know what I mean?
(at the concert)

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: You know what? I'm not gonna be able to enjoy this.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Yeah, I know, it's my birthday. We all should be here.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: So, let's go.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Well maybe, you know, maybe we should stay for one song.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah, I mean, it would be rude to them for us to leave now.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: You know, the guys are probably having a great time.
(at Monica and Rachel's)

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Come on you guys, one more time.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok. One.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Nooo.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: That was amazing!

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Excellent, that was excellent.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I can't believe the guys missed this.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: What guys? Oh, yeah.

lines.speaker: STEVE
lines.text: Excuse me, you're Monica Geller aren't you?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Do I know you?

lines.speaker: STEVE
lines.text: You used to be my babysitter.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Oh my god, little Stevie Fisher? How've you been?

lines.speaker: STEVE
lines.text: Good, good, I'm a lawyer now.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: You can't be a lawyer. You're eight.

lines.speaker: STEVE
lines.text: Listen, it was nice to see you. I gotta run backstage.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Uh, wait, backstage?

lines.speaker: STEVE
lines.text: Oh, yeah, my firm represents the band.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ross.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Chandler.

lines.speaker: STEVE
lines.text: How are you? Look, you guys wanna meet the group? Come on. So, are you one of
the ones who fooled around with my dad?
(at Central Perk)

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hey, you guys.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Happy birthday.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Oh, thank you, thanks. So uh, how was your night last night?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Oh, well, it pretty much sucked. How was yours?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Yeah, ours pretty much sucked, oh, but, I did run into little Stevie Fisher.
Remember him?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Oh yeah. I used to babysit him. Hey, how's his dad?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Uh, good.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Uh, aside from that, the whole evening was pretty much a bust.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah, we really missed you guys.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Yeah, look, we were just saying, this whole thing is really stupid.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: We just have to really, really, really, not let stuff like money get--is that a
hickey?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: No, I just, I fell down.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: On someone's lips? Where'd you get the hickey?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: You know, a party, or--

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What party?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: It wasn't so much a party as...a gathering of people, with food, and music, and,
and the band.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You partied with Hootie and the Blowfish?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yes, apparently Stevie and the band are like this.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Who gave you that hickey?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: That would be the work of a Blowfish.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Oh!

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh! I can't believe it. I can't believe this. We're just like, sitting at home,
trying to guess Joey's fingers, and you guys are out like partying and having fun, and you
know, all, "hey, Blowfish, suck on my neck".

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Look, don't blame us. You guys coulda been there, you know.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What, as part of your poor friends outreach program?
(Monica's pager goes off)

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: It's work.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I don't know what to say. I'm sorry that we make more money than you. But
we're not gonna feel guilty about it. We work really hard for it.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: And we don't work hard?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: (on phone) Yeah, hi, it's Monica. I just got a page.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I'm just saying that sometimes we like to do stuff that costs a little more.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: And you feel like we hold you back.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Oh!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Leon, Leon. Shhh! Guys. Wait, I don't understand. Those steaks were just a gift
from the meat vendor. That was not a kick back. I'll just replace them and we can forget
the whole thing. What corporate policy? No. Yeah. All right. I just got fired.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh.
(Everyone goes over to comfort Monica)

lines.speaker: WAITRESS
lines.text: Here's your check. That'll be $4.12.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Let me get that. (to Chandler) You got five bucks?

lines.speaker: MACHINE
lines.text: Here comes the beep, you know what to do.

lines.speaker: JADE
lines.text: Hi, it's me. Listen, Bob. I'm probably way out of line here. I mean, It has been
3 years, and you're probably seeing someone else now, but if we could just have one night
together, just for old time's sake, one hot, steamy, wild night...
(Joey lunges for phone and misses.)
END

title: The One with the Baby on the Bus

scenes.location: At Monica and Rachel's.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Who da wenny-Benny boy? You the Wenny-wenny-Benny-Benny boy, yes. Don't cry. Don't
cry. Why is he still crying?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Let me hold him for a sec. There. (Ben stops crying) Huh? There we are.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Maye it's me.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Don't be silly. Ben loves you. He's just being Mr. Crankypants.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You know, I once dated a Miss Crankypants. Lovely girl, kinda moody.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: There we go. All better. (gives Ben back to Monica)

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: There's my little boy. (Ben starts crying again)

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Can I uh see something? (Takes Ben. When he puts him close to Monica, Ben cries.
When he moves Ben away, he stops crying.)

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Cool.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: He hates me. My nephew hates me.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Come on, don't do this.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: What if my own baby hates me? Huh? What am I gonna do then?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Monica, will you stop? This is nuts. Do you know how long it's gonna be before
you actually have to deal with this problem? I mean, you don't even have a boyfriend yet.
Joey, she does not look fat.
(Chandler has a basketball which he is moving closer to, then away from, Monica)

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Goo, goo, goo, waaah!

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: That is so funny. Let me see that. (throws the ball out the window)

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Are you ok, Ross?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I don't know. What's in this pie?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Uh, I don't know, butter, eggs, flour, lime, kiwi--

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Kiwi? Kiwi? I thought it was a key lime pie.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: No I didn't, I said kiwi lime. That's what makes it so special.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And that's what's gonna kill me. I'm allergic to kiwi.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: No you're not. You're, you're allergic to lobster and peanuts and--oh my god.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ugh.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Oh my god.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ugh. It's definitely getting worse.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Is your tongue swelling up?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Either that or my mouth is getting smaller.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: All right, get your coat, we're going to the hospital.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Is he gonna be ok?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Yeah, he's just gotta get a shot.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You know, you know, actually it's getting better. It is. It is. Let's not go. Anyone
for Thcrabble?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Jacket now.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: What about Ben? We can't bring a baby to a hospital.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: We'll watch him.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I don't think tho.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: What? I have seven Catholic sisters. I've taken care of hundreds of kids. Come on,
we wanna do it, don't we?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: I was looking forward to playing basketball, but I guess that's out the window.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ok, well, if you do take him out for his walk, you might wanna bring his hat, and
there's extra milk in the fridge, and there's extra diapers in the bag.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hat, milk, got it.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: ??? (speech garbled) Thro up a thro thro--a thro thro!

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Consider it done.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You understood that?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Yeah, my uncle Sal has a really big tongue.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Is he the one with the beautiful wife?
(Central Perk)

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Hey Rach, wanna hear the new song I'm thinkin' of singing this afternoon? I wrote
it this morning in the shower.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: (singing) I'm in the shower and I'm writing a song. Stop me if you've heard it. My
skin is soapy, and my hair is wet, and Tegrin spelled backward is Nirget.

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: Uh, Rachel, sweetheart, could I see ya for a minute?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What's up?

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: F.Y.I.. I've decided to pay a professional musician to play in here on Sunday
afternoons. Her name is Stephanie... something. She's supposed to be very good.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: But what about Phoebe?

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: Rachel, it's not that your friend is bad, it's that she's so bad, she makes me want
to put my finger through my eye into my brain and swirl it around.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok, ok, so you're not a fan, but I mean, come on, you cannot do this to her.

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: Uh--

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Oh, no no no no. Oh no no no no. I have to do this to her?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: (singing) Lather, rinse, repeat, and lather, rinse, repeat, and lather, rinse,
repeat, as needed.
(Chandler and Joey are loaded down with baby stuff, and Ben)

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You know, I don't think we brought enough stuff. Did you forget to pack the
baby's anvil?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: It's gonna be worth it. It's a known fact that women love babies, all righ? Women
love guys who love babies. It's that whole sensitive thing. Quick, aim him at that pack o'
babes over there. Maybe one of them will break away. No, no wait, for get them, we got
one, hard left. All right, gimme the baby.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: No, I got him.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: No, seriously.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Oh, seriously you want him?

lines.speaker: CAROLINE
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: BOYS
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: CAROLINE
lines.text: And who is this little cutie pie?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Well, don't, don't think me immodest, but, me?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You wanna smell him?

lines.speaker: CAROLINE
lines.text: I assume we're talking about the baby now.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Oh, yeah. He's got that great baby smell. Get a whiff of his head.

lines.speaker: CAROLINE
lines.text: I think my uterus just skipped a beat.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: (to Chandler) What'd I tell you? What'd I tell you?

lines.speaker: CAROLINE
lines.text: I think it's great you guys are doing this.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Well, we are great guys.

lines.speaker: CAROLINE
lines.text: You know, my brother and his boyfriend have been trying to adopt for three
years. What agency did you two go through?
(Central Perk)

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But, but this is my gig. This is where I play. My, my name is written out there in
chalk. You know, you can't just erase chalk.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Honey, I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And he's going to be paying this woman? Why doesn't he just give her like a
throne, and a crown, and like a, you know, gold stick with a ball on top.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Terry is a jerk, ok? That's why we're always saying "Terry's a jerk!"
That's where that came from.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Yeah, ok. You probably did everything you could.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok, you know what, lemme, let me just see what else I can do. All right, look,
look. Why don't you just let her go on after Stephanie whatever-her-name-is. I mean, you
won't even be here. You don't pay her. It's not gonna cost you anything.

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: I, I don't know.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Come on, Terry, I'll even clean the cappuccino machine.

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: You don't clean the cappuccino machine?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Of course I clean it. I mean, I,I will cleeeean it. I mean, I will cleeeean it.

lines.speaker: TERRY
lines.text: Oh, all right, fine, fine, fine.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Done.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Yeah. Who's workin' for you babe?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh! Oh my god. This is so exciting. How much am I gonna get?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Well you said that he's paying the people who are playing.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Oh, no, no no. I meant that he's gonna be paying that other woman beause she's a
professional.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Well, I'm not gonna be the only one who's not getting paid.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Well, but Pheebs.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: No, huh uh, I'm sorry, no. No, I'm not some like sloppy second, charity band. You
know what, there are thousands of places in this city where people would be happy to pay
to hear me play. (Out on the sidewalk, singing) When I play, I play for me, I don't need
your charity. (Someone puts a coin in her guitar case) Thank you! La la la la la la la....

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Well, there's no way I'm gonna get a shot. Maybe they can take the needle and
thquirt it into my mouth, you know, like a thquirt gun.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Hello, there. I'm Dr. Carlin. I see someone's having an allergic reaction.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Doctor, can I see you for just a minute please? My brother has a slight phobia
about needles.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Did you tell him about my thquirt gun idea?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: My brother, the PhD would like to know if there's any way to treat this orally.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: No, under these circumstances it has to be an injection, and it has to be now.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Tho?
(Monica shakes her head.)

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ohhh.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: That's good, have a seat. Um, the doctor says it's gotta be a needle. You're just
gonna have to be brave, ok? Can you do that for me?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ok.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Ok. Oh boy. You are doin' so good. You wanna squeeze my hand? All right, Ross,
don't squeeze it so hard. Honey, really, don't squeeze it so hard! Oh, Ross! Let go of my
hand!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: That's a good plan, Joe. Next time we wanna pick up women, we should just go to
the park and make out. Taxi, taxi!

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, hey, look at that talent.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: (to taxi driver) Just practicing. You're good. Carry on.
GIRL 1 ON BUS: Hey, you. He's just adorable.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Ok, but can you tell him that, because he thinks he's too pink.
GIRL 2 ON BUS: So what are you guys out doing today?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Oh we're not out. No, no. We're just uh, two heterosexual guys, hanging with the son
of our other heterosexual friend, doin' the usual straight guy stuff.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You done?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Yeah.
GIRL 1: Oh, there's our stop.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Get outta here. This is our stop too.
GIRL 2: You guys live around here too?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, sure. We live in the building by the uh sidewalk.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: You know it?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, look, since we're neighbors and all, what do you say we uh, get together for a
drink?
GIRL 1: So uh, you wanna go to Marquel's?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Oh, sure, they love us over there.
GIRL 2: Where's your baby?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER AND JOEY
lines.text: (running after bus) Ben! Ben! Ben!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Oh, that's good. Maybe he'll hear you and pull the cord.

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: Stop the bus! Wait! Wait! Wait!

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Are you sure he didn't break it because it really hurts.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: No, it's just a good bone bruise. And, right here is the puncture wound from your
ring.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm really sorry. Sorry. Sorry! Hey! Hey! I got my s's back! Which we
can celebrate later. Celebrate.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: (singing) ... with the double double double-jointed boy. Hey. So um, are you the
professional guitar player?

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: Yeah. I'm Stephanie.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Right. My name was on there, but now it just says "carrot cake". So, um,
so um, how many chords do you know?

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: All of them.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh yeah, so you know D?

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok, do you know A minor?

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok, do you know how to go from D to A minor?

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ok. Um, so does your guitar have a strap?

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh. Mine does. (singing) Stephanie knows all the chords. (makes a face)

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: (on pay phone) Come on, pick up, pick up! Hello? Transit Authority? Yes, hello.
I'm doing research for a book, and I was wondering what someone might do if they left a
baby on a city bus. Yes I do realize that would be a very stupid charact er.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hi, here's the deal. We lost a carseat on a bus today. It's white plastic, with a
handle, and it fits onto a stroller. Oh, and there was a baby in it. He wants to talk to
you again.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ok, everybody, let's give a uh nice warm Central Perk welcome to--

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: (singing angrily) Terry's a jerk, and he won't let me work, and I hate Central
Perk!

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Uh, to Stephanie Schiffer.

lines.speaker: STEPHANIE
lines.text: Thank you. I'd like to start with a song that I wrote for the first man I ever
loved. (singing) Zachary.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: (singing/screaming) You're all invited to bite me!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER AND JOEY
lines.text: Hi. We're the guys who called about the baby. We left the baby on ths
bus. Is he here? Is he here?

lines.speaker: TRANSIT AUTHORITY GUY
lines.text: He's here. (Chandler and Joey hug each other in relief) I'm
assuming one of you is the father.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: That's me.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: I'm him.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Actually, uh, we're both the father. (Puts his arm around Joey)
BOTH (but to different babies): Oh, Ben! Hey, buddy!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Please tell me you know which one is our baby.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Well, well that one has ducks on his t-shirt, and this one has clowns. And Ben was
definitely wearing ducks.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Ok.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Or clowns. Oh, oh wait. That one's definitely Ben. Remember, he had that cute little
mole by his mouth.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Hey, Ben, remember us? Ok, the mole came off.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Ahh!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: What're we gonna do? What're we gonna do?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Uh, uh, we'll flip for it. Ducks or clowns.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Oh, we're gonna flip for the baby?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You got a better idea?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: All right, call it in the air.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Heads.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Heads it is.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Yes! Whew!

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: We have to assign heads to something.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Right. Ok, ok, uh, ducks is heads, because ducks have heads.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: What kind of scary-ass clowns came to your birthday?
(on the sidewalk outside Central Perk)

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Oh, hi.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Here. I thought you might be cold.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Whoa, look at you, you did pretty well.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Eight dollars and 27 cents. But not really, 'cause I put in the first two, just
to, you know, get the ball rolling, and to make myself feel better.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Do you?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: No. This whole like playing-for-money thing is so not good for me. You know, I
don't know, when I sang "Su-Su-Suicide", I got a dollar seventy-five. But then,
"Smelly Cat", I got 25 cents and a condom. So you know, now I just feel really
bad for Smelly Cat.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Well, you know, honey, I don't think everybody gets Smelly Cat. You know, I mean,
if all you've ever actually had are healthy pets, then, whoosh!

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: It's not even that. I used to do my songs because it made me happy, but now it's
like, it's just all about the money.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Well, people missed you in there. And in fact, there was actually a request for
"Smelly Cat".

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Really? From who?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Well, from me. And I know it's not your big money song, but it's my favorite.

lines.speaker: KID
lines.text: Hi. Uh, did I accidentally drop a condom in your case? It's kind of an emergency.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Yeah. Here you go.

lines.speaker: KID
lines.text: Thanks a lot. Hey Christine, I got it!
(chez Monica and Rachel)

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I just wanna thank you for being there for me today. And I'm sorry I,I almost broke
your hand.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: That's ok. I'm sorry I poisoned you.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Yeah. Hey, remember the time I jammed that pencil into your hand?

[Rachel slams the door and locks it. She sits down, visibly upset. She puts her head in
her hands and begins to cry. Ross comes back and is standing outside the window. When
Rachel regroups and gets back up to finish closing, she sees him. She smiles. She goes to
open the door and can't get the lock undone.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Try the bottom one.
[She opens the door and they kiss.]

scenes.location: Chandler and Joey's apartment. Chandler answers the door to find Monica.

lines.text: CLOSING CREDITS

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Monica, it's 6:30 in the morning. We're not working out, it's over.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: No way, with one pound to go, c'mon. We're workin', we're movin', we're in the zone
we're groovin'.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: OK, I don't, I don't mind the last pound. OK, in fact I kind of like the last pound.
OK, so don't make me do anything that I'll regret.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Ooh, what'cha gonna do, fat boy, huh? What?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Nothing, except tell you, uh, I think it's wonderful how much energy you have.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Well, thanks.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: I mean, especially considering how tough it's been for you to find work.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Well, you know.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: You know, I mean, you can't tell your parents you were fired because they'd be
disappointed.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [sad] Uh-huh.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: And it's not as if you have a boyfriend's shoulder to cry on.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Well no, but um.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: I mean, if it were me, I think I'd have difficulty just getting out of bed at all.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Y'know, I try to stay positive. . .

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: So, you feel like goin' for a run?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Alright.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Because, you know, you don't have to. If you want, you could just take a nap right
here.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: OK. Just for a little while.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: OK. [Puts an afghan over her and dances into his room]
END

title: The One with the List

lines.text: [Scene: Monica and Rachel's apartment. Phoebe, Monica, and Rachel are there, discussing
the night before.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Ross kissed me.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Oh my god, oh my god, oh my god!

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: It was unbelievable!

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Oh my god, oh my god, oh my god!

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Ok, all right. We want to hear everything. Monica, get the wine and unplug the
phone. Rachel, does this end well or do we need to get tissues?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh, it ended very well.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [getting the wine] Do not start without me. Do not start without me.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Ok, all right, let's hear about the kiss. Was it like, was it like a soft brush
against your lips? Or was it like a, you know, a "I gotta have you now" kind of
thing?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Well, at first it was really intense, you know. And then, oh, god, and then we
just sort of sunk into it.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Ok, so, ok, was he holding you? Or was his hand like on your back?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: No, actually first they started on my waist. And then, they slid up, and then,
they were in my hair.
PHOE/MNCA: Ohhhh.

scenes.location: Ross' apartment. Ross, Chandler, and Joey are there eating pizza.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And, uh, and then I kissed her.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Tongue?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Cool.
Opening Credits
[Scene: Central Perk. Joey, Phoebe, Monica, and Chandler are there; Chandler is
showing everyone his new computer.]

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: All right, check out this bad boy. 12 megabytes of ram. 500 megabyte hard drive.
Built-in spreadsheet capabilities and a modem that transmits at over 28,000 b.p.s.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Wow. What are you gonna use it for?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: [doggedly] Games and stuff.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [reading the paper] There are no jobs. There are no jobs for me.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: [reading over her shoulder] Wait, here's one. Uh, would you be willing to cook
naked?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: There's an ad for a naked chef?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: No, but if you're willing to cook naked, then you might be willing to dance
naked. And then... [rubs his fingers together]
[Ross enters, distraught.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Hey, oh, so, um...how'd you make out last night?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: That, that is funny. That is painfully funny. No, wait. Wait, yeah, that's just
painful

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Wait a minute. I thought last night was great.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Yeah, it was, but...I get home, ok, and I see Julie's saline solution on my night
table. And I'm thinking to myself, oh my god, what the hell am I doing? I mean, here I am,
I am with Julie, this incredible, great woman, who I care about and who cares about me,
and I'm like, what, am I just gonna throw all that away?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You got all that from saline solution?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: We are talking about Rachel here. You and Rachel.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Believe me, I've been dreaming about me and Rachel for ten years now. But now,
I'm with Julie, so it's like me and Julie, me and Rachel, me and Julie, me and... [Rachel
enters, carrying a tray]... Rachel. Rachel, Rachel.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: [to Ross] Hey, you.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: How are you?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Good. How are you?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Good.
[Julie enters.]

lines.speaker: JULIE
lines.text: Hi, honey.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hi, Julie. [nervous] Hi, Julie. Julie, um, how are you?

lines.speaker: JULIE
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: [uncomfortable] Good, so everybody's here. Everybody's good. So, were you gonna
play something, Phoebe?

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Oh, well, actually.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: [impatient] Play it.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Ok, all right.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, Julie, I didn't know you wore lenses.

lines.speaker: JULIE
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: [to Joey] Ssshh.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Ok, um, hi, hello, hi, ok, so, um, this is a song about a love triangle between
three people that I made up. Um, it's called, um, "Two of Them Kissed Last
Night".
[Ross and Rachel look at each other and then at Phoebe, realizing the song is about
their situation.]

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: [singing] There was a girl, we'll call her Betty, and a guy let's call him Neil.
Now I can't stress this point too strongly, this story isn't real. Now our Neil must
decide, who will be the girl that he casts aside. Will Betty be the one who he loves
truly? Or will it be the one who we'll call Ju...Loolie? He must decide, he must decide,
even though I made him up, he must decide!

scenes.location: Mr. Ratstatter's (RTST) office. Monica is there about a job.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: This is a nice resume. Nice, nice, nice. Muy impressivo.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: So, Mr. Rastatter, what exactly does this job entail? The ad wasn't too clear.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Mockolate.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: I'm sorry?

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Mockolate. It's a completely synthetic chocolate substitute.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Ohh.
[He pulls out a piece of Mockolate.]

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Go ahead. Try a piece. Yeah, we think that Mockolate is even better than
chocolate.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: All right. Mmm-mmm.
[She tastes it, and obviously hates it.]

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Yeah?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [disgusted, trying not to show it] I love how it crumbles. Now see, your
chocolate doesn't do that.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: No, ma'am. Well, anyhoo, we should be getting our F.D.A. approval any day now,
hopefully, in time for Thanksgiving. See, the way we look at it, chocolate already
dominates most of your major food-preparation holidays: Easter, Christmas, what have you.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [still chewing] Mmm-mmm.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: But, we're thinking, given the right marketing, we can make Thanksgiving the
Mockolate holiday.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Aren't you going to swallow that?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Just waiting for it to stop bubbling.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Yeah, isn't that great?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [with false enthusiasm] Mmm.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Well, anyhoo, um, we are looking for a couple of chefs who can create some
Thanksgiving-themed recipes. You think you might be interested?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Abso...[swallows hard]...lutely. See, I love creating new recipes. I love
Thanksgiving. And, well, now, I love Mockolate.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Especially the after taste, you know, I'll tell ya, that'll last ya till
Christmas.
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's apartment. Monica and Phoebe are there. Monica is
suggesting Mockolate recipes to Phoebe.]

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: How about Mockolate mousse?

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: It's not, it's not very Thanksgiving-y.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Ok, how about pilgrim Mockolate mousse?

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: What makes it pilgrim?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: We'll put buckles on it.
[Rachel enters.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Did uh, Ross call?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: No, I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Why didn't he call? He's gonna stay with Julie, isn't he? He's gonna stay with
her and she's going to be all, "Hi, I'm Julie, Ross picked me, and we're gonna to get
married, have a lot of kids and dig up stuff together."

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: No offense, but that sounds nothing like her.
[Scene: Chandler and Joey's apartment. Ross is up in arms about the Rachel/Julie
situation.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I don't know what to do. What am I gonna do? I mean, this, this is like a
complete nightmare.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Oh, I know. This must be so hard. Oh, no. Two women love me. They're both
gorgeous and sexy. My wallet's too small for my fifties, and my diamond shoes are too
tight.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, here's a thought, Ross. [reaches for the computer]

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Don't touch the computer. Don't ever touch the computer.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Ross, listen. I got two words for you. Threesome.
[Ross gives him an insulted look.]

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Ok, all right, look. Let's get logical about this, ok? We'll make a list. Rachel
and Julie, pros and cons. Oh. We'll put their names in bold, with different fonts, and I
can use different colors for each column.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Can't we just use a pen?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: No, Amish boy.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Ok, let's start with the cons, 'cause they're more fun. All right, Rachel first.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I don't know. I mean, all right, I guess you can say she's a little spoiled
sometimes.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You could say that.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And I guess, you know, sometimes, she's a little ditzy, you know. And I've seen
her be a little too into her looks. Oh, and Julie and I, we have a lot in common 'cause
we're both paleontologists, but Rachel's just a waitress.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Waitress. Got it. You guys wanna play Doom? Or we could keep doing this. What
else?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Oh, her ankles are a little chubby.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Ok, let's do Julie. What's wrong with her?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: [long pause] She's not Rachel.
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's apartment. Monica has made food for Phoebe and Rachel to
taste.]

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Ok, this is pumpkin pie with mockolate cookie crumb crust. This is mockolate
cranberry cake, and these are mockolate chip cookies. Just like the Indians served.
[Rachel takes a bite.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh my god.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Oh my god good?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh my god, I can't believe you let me put this in my mouth.
[Rachel runs to the sink to spit it out.]

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Oh, oh sweet Lord! This is what evil must taste like!
[Scene: Chandler and Joey's apartment. Chandler is on the phone with a computer
hotline.]

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: I'm telling you this thing won't print. Yes, I pressed that button like 100
times. You know, for a hot line you are not so hot. What? What is that in the background?
Are you watching Star Trek?
[Ross enters with a melancholy look.]

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: [to Ross] Hey, so how'd it go with Julie? Did you, did you break her heart?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Yes, it was horrible. She cried. I cried. She threw things, they hit me. Anyway,
I did the right thing.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: [in phone] So, Spock actually hugs his father?
[Rachel enters.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Hey, do you guys have...[sees Ross, pauses]...hi.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: [sees his coat on] Where you goin'?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I uh, I just got back from uh, from Julie's.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: [dejected] Oh.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, no, uh, it's not what you think. It's um the other thing.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Well, what's the other thing, what do I think?
[Joey is looking at Rachel, smiling, and gesturing his head towards Ross.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Well, uh.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: He broke up with Julie. Well, go hug her, for god's sakes.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Really. It's always been you, Rach.
[Ross and Rachel hug.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh, god.
JOEY/CHAN: Ohhh.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh, oh, this is good, this is really good.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I know, I know, it's, it's almost...[turns around, sees Chandler and Joey] What
do you say we go take a walk, just us, not them?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Let me get my coat.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ok. No, hey, whoa, whoa, I'll get your coat.
[Ross leaves.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Ok, he's goin' to get my coat. He's goin' to get my coat. Oh my god, you guys. I
can't believe this. This is unbelievable. [notices Chandler's computer screen] What's
that?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: [nervous] What? Nothing.
[Chandler closes up the laptop computer screen.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: What's that? What? I saw my name. What is it?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: No, no, see? See? [the printer starts to run] Hey, it's printing. [to Joey,
rattled] Hey, it's printing!
[Chandler rips off the sheet of paper from the printer.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Well what is it? Let me see.
[Ross walks back in, Rachel's coat in hand.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hey, someone order a coat?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Ross, Chandler wrote something about me on his computer and he won't let me see.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: He won't? [remembers what it is] He won't! Because, isn't that, isn't that the,
the short story you were writing?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Yes, yes it is, short story, that I was writing.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: And I'm in it? Then let me read it.
CHAN, JOEY, ROSS: No!

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Come on.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, uh, why don't you read it to her?
[Ross and Chandler stare angrily at Joey, who thinks he has come up with a good idea.]

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: [through gritted teeth] Alright. [clears his throat] "It was summer, and it
was hot. Rachel was there. A lonely gray couch. 'Oh, look,' cried Ned, and then the
kingdom was his forever. The end."

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: That's it? That's all you wrote? You're the worst writer in the whole world.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: All right, you know what? This isn't funny anymore. There's something about me on
that piece of paper and I want to see it.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, you don't.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: All right, you know what, that's fine. If you guys want to be children about
this, that's fine. I do not need to see it. [Rachel grabs the paper and runs across the
room, reading it to herself.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: What is this? Ross, what is this?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Good luck.
[Chandler and Joey leave quickly.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ok, just, just remember how crazy I am about you, ok?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Kind of ditzy? Too into her looks? Spoiled?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Now that's a little spoiled. He was supposed to type "little", the
idiot.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Just a waitress?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, that, that was, I mean, as opposed to uh, the uh, ok. Is this over yet Rach?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh! I do not have chubby ankles!
[Rachel leaves, and Ross follows her into the hall.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, no, wait, ok, ok, look at the other side. Look at Julie's column.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: She is not Rachem. What the hell's a Rachem? Is that some stupid
paleontology word that I wouldn't know because I'm just a waitress.
[She goes into her apartment and slams the door.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, Rach, come on. Rach! Rach, no, no! She's not Rachel, she is, she is not,
Ra--Rachel?

scenes.location: Central Perk. Chandler, Monica, Joey, and Phoebe are there.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: My diary! My diary, that's brilliant. I should have told her it was my diary, she
never would have made me read her my diary.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: You know, that's true. You'd be a great person to have around the day after an
emergency.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: I... I cannot believe Ross even made this list. What a dinkus.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, cut him some slack. It was Chandler's idea.

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Oh good, I was hoping that would come up.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: This was your idea?

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: What were you thinking?

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: [squirming] All right, let's get some perspective here, ok? These things, they
happen for a reason.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Yeah. You!

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: All right, Pheebs, back me up here, ok? You believe in that karma crap, don't
you?

lines.speaker: PHOE
lines.text: Yeah, by the way, good luck in your next life as a dung beetle.
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's apartment. Rachel is sitting on the couch, eating candy. It
is raining out. Ross climbs up the fire escape and is knocking on the window.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Rach! Whoops! Rach, hey, open up, please!

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: [coldly] When somebody does not buzz you in, Ross, that means go away. That
doesn't mean please climb up the fire escape.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I just wanna read something. It's your pro list.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Not interested.
[Rachel closes the drapes over the window, goes into her bedroom and closes the door.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: [reading his list] Ok, ok, number one: The way you cry at game shows. Number two:
how much you love your friends. Number three: the way you play with your hair when you're
nervous. Number four: how brave you are for starting your life over. Number five: how
great you are with Ben.
[Monica, Chandler, Joey, and Phoebe enter, confused.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Number six: the way you smell.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: [opens the drapes] Hey, Ross! What are you doin'?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hey, Joey. You wanna open the window?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Oh, yeah, I do.
[He opens the window, Ross comes in, soaked.]

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: What are you doing out there?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I am, uh, I am...

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Oh, you must be freezing. You know what you need? How about a nice steaming cup
of hot Mockolate?
[Ross runs to Rachel's bedroom, knocking on the door.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Rach, come on, open up. Rach, come on, come on, Rach. You got to give me another
chance.
[Rachel opens the door.]

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: That's what I said.

lines.speaker: CHAN
lines.text: Look, maybe we should go?

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: No, you guys, you really don't have to go, we're done talking.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Rach, come on, look, I know how you must feel.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: [near tears] No, you don't, Ross. Imagine the worst things you think about
yourself. Now, how would you feel if the one person that you trusted the most in the world
not only thinks them too, but actually uses them as reasons not to be with you.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No, but, but I wanna be with you in spite of all those things.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Oh, well, that's, that's mighty big of you, Ross. [to the others] I said don't
go!

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You know what? You know what? If, things were the other way around, there's
nothing you could put on a list that would ever make me not want to be with you.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: Well, then, I guess that's the difference between us. See, I'd never make a list.
[She closes the door in his face. Ross walks sullenly back to the couch and sits down.
A moment of silence ensues.]

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: [quietly] I never know how long you're supposed to wait in this type of a
situation before you can talk again, you know? [Ross stares blankly at him] Maybe a little
longer.

scenes.location: Mr. Ratstatter's office. Monica is there.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Now, in some of these recipes, the quantities may seem just a little unusual, uh,
like these coconut mockolate holiday nut bars. I've indicated four cups of coconut, and
four cups of crushed nut, and only, uh, one tablespoon of mockolate.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Doesn't matter.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Our FDA approval didn't come through. Something about laboratory rats.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Oh, gosh, I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Yeah, well, anyhoo, here is your check. [hands it to her] Thank you for all the
trouble you went through. Um, listen, you didn't eat a lot of it while you were cooking,
did you?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Well, uh, I ate some.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Oh, some, that's fine. Some is fine. Some is not a lot. So, it doesn't burn when
you pee, does it?

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's apartment. Monica and Rachel are there.

lines.text: (phone rings)

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Hello?
[Ross is at his apartment.]

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: RACH
lines.text: [to Monica] Is that him again? Tell him I'd come to the phone, but my ankles are
weighin' me down.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: [to Ross] Listen, I... I don't think this is the best time.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Look, can, can you do something for me?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Sure, what? Ok, ok. [hangs up the phone] [to Rachel] Music?
[Monica turns on the radio.]

lines.speaker: RADIO
lines.text: The next one's dedicated to Rachel from Ross. Rachel, he wants you to know he's
deeply sorry for what he did and he hopes you can find it in your heart to forgive him. (With
or Without You plays)
[Rachel seems touched. She pauses for a moment, then picks up the phone and starts to
dial. Cut to Ross at his apartment.]

lines.speaker: RADIO
lines.text: Uh, we've just gotten a call from Rachel, and she told us what Ross did. It's
pretty appalling, and Ross, if you're listening, I don't wanna play your song anymore. Why
don't we devote our time to a couple that stands a chance? Avery, Michelle's sorry she hit
you with her car and she hopes you two will work it out.

scenes.location: Mr. Ratstatter's office. Monica is there.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Hi, thanks for coming in again.

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Oh, not at all. I have no morals and I need the cash.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: It's like I'm lookin' in a mirror. Anyway, they're called
"fishtachios". They taste exactly like pistachios, but they're made primarily of
reconstituted fish bits. Here, try one. You're not allergic to anything, are you?

lines.speaker: MNCA
lines.text: Cat hair.

lines.speaker: RTST
lines.text: Oh, sorry.
END

title: The One with Phoebe's Dad

lines.text: [Scene: Monica and Rachel's apartment. Monica, Rachel, Ross, and Phoebe
are there. Phoebe is looking out the window.]

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ooh, ooh, ooh, ooh, ooh. Ugly Naked Guy is decorating his tree. Oh my God, you
should see the size of his Christmas Balls.
[Chandler and Joey enter.]

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Hey, how much did you guys tip the super this year?

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Yeah, we were gonna give fifty, but if you guys gave more, we don't wanna look
bad.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Oh, actually this year we just made him homemade cookies.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: And twenty-five it is.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: You gave him cookies?

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Money is so impersonal. Cookies says someone really cares. . . Alright, we're
broke, but cookies do say that.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I can see that. A plate of brownies once told me a limerick.

lines.speaker: CHANDLER
lines.text: Phoebs, let me ask you something, were, were these, uh, funny brownies?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Not especially. But you know what, I think they had pot in them.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: So you guys, who else did you tip with cookies?

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Uhh, the mailman, the super.
[There's a bang at the door.]

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Oh, and the newspaper delivery guy.
[Joey opens the door and picks up the remnants of the newspaper.

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Oh my God.

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: JOEY
lines.text: Uhhh, I don't think you're gonna like this.
[Joey shows them the torn-up newspaper.]

lines.speaker: RACHEL
lines.text: Ooh, goooosh, ooh, these are cookies smashed in the sports section.

lines.speaker: MONICA
lines.text: Oh look, and he did my crossword puzzle.

lines.speaker: ROSS
