lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: All right here. Watch me execute the three ‘P’s of championship
play. Power. (swings the racquet) Precision. (swings the racquet.) and penache. (does a
backswing and hits Sarah who’s started up the stairs, knocking her down, they both
watch in horror.)

scenes.location: Central Perk, the gang’s all there discussing the incident.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: You broke a little girl’s leg?!!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I know. I feel horrible. Okay.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (reading the paper) Says here that a muppet got whacked on Seasame
Street last night. (to Ross) Where exactly were around ten-ish?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well, I’m gonna go see her. I want to bring her something, what do
you think she’ll like?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Maybe a Hello Kitty doll, the ability to walk...
(Rachel starts to laugh, and Ross notices her.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I’m gonna get back to retraining. (gets up)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: All right, see you guys. (starts to leave)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Look out kids, he’s coming! (Ross continues to leave with his
head down in shame.)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: And I gotta go sell some Christmas trees.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Have fun. Oh wait, no, don’t! I forgot I am totally against that
now.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: What? Me having a job?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: No, no, I am against innocent trees being cut down in their prime, and
their, their corpses grotesquely dressed in like tinsel and twinkly lights. (to Joey) Hey,
how do you sleep at night?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Well, I’m pretty tired from lugging the trees around all day. Hey,
Phoebe listen, you got this all wrong. Those trees were born to be Christmas trees, their
fulfilling their life purpose, by, by making people happy.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Really?
(Phoebe turns and looks at Monica, while Joey frantically motions to Chandler to help
him out.)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yes. Yes, and ah, ah, the trees are happy too, because for most of
them, it’s the only chance to see New York.
[cut to Gunther retraining Rachel.]

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: ...and after you’ve delivered the drinks, you take the empty
tray....

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Gunther, Gunther, please, I’ve worked here for two and a half
years, I know the empty trays go over there. (points to the counter.)

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: What if you put them here. (sets the empty tray on another stack of
empty trays on the back counter.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Huh. Well, y'know that’s actually a really good idea, because that
way they’ll be closer to the mugs. Y'know what, you should have the other waitresses
do that too.

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: They already do. That’s why they call it the ‘tray

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Gee, I always heard them talk about that, I just always thought that it
was a club they went to. Oh God, I’m, I’m sorry. (walks away)

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: It’s all right. Sweetheart.

scenes.location: Sarah’s bedroom, her room is decorated with a space motif.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: So, this must be kinda neat for ya, huh? I mean, your Dad tells me that
you get a couple of days off school, and you, you ah, don’t have to sell those
cookies anymore.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Well, I kinda wanted to sell the cookies. The girl who sells the most
wins a trip to Spacecamp, and gets to sit in a real space shuttle.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Wow, you ah, you really like all this space stuff, huh?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yeah. My Dad says if I spend as much time helping him clean apartments,
as I do daydreaming about outer space, he’d be able to afford a trip to the Taj
Mahal.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I think you would have to clean a whole lot of apartments to go all the
way to India.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: No. The one in Atlantic City, Dad loves the slots. He says he’s
gonna double the college money my Grandma left me.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Huh. Well, good luck to Dad. Say, how many more boxes would you have to
sell in order to win?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: The girl who won last year sold four hundred and seventy-five.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So far, I’ve sold seventy-five.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Four hundred, huh? Well, that sounds do-able. (starts to get out his
wallet) How much are the boxes?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Five dollars a box.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (puts away his wallet) And what is second prize?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: A ten speed bike. But, I’d rather have something my Dad
couldn’t sell.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well, that makes sense.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Could you do me one favor, if it’s not too much trouble?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah, Sarah, anything.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Could you pull open the curtains for me? The astronauts from the space
shuttle are gonna be on the news, and since we don’t have a TV, the lady across the
alley said she’d push hers up to a window, so I could watch it.
[Scene: A hallway, Ross is selling Brown Bird cookies for Sarah, he stops and knocks on
a door.]

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: (looking through her peephole, we see Ross standing in the hallway.)
Yesss?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi, I’m selling Brown Bird cookies.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: You’re no Brown Bird, I can see you through my peephole.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No, hi, I’m, I’m an honorary Brown Bird (does the Brown Bird
salute.)

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: What does that mean?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah, well, it means that I can sell cookies, but I’m not invited to
sleep-overs.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I can dial 9-1-1 at the touch of a button, y'know. Now, go away!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No, please, please, um, it’s for a poor little girl who wants to go
to Spacecamp more than anything in the world.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I’m pressing, a policeman is on his way.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Okay, okay! I’m going. I’m going. (goes across the hall to knock
on another door.)

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I can still see you!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: All right!!

scenes.location: Joey’s work, selling Christmas trees.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (walking up to Joey) Hey.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Hey. What, what are you doing here?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well, I-I thought a lot about what you said, and um, I realilized duh,
all right maybe I was a little judgmental. Yeah, (looks at the tree) oh, but oh...

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Look now, Phoebe remember, hey, their just fulfilling their Christmas....

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Destiny.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Okay. (One of Joey’s co-workers, walks by with a dead tree.) Yikes!
That one doesn’t look very fulfilled.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Oh, that’s, that’s ah, one of the old ones, he’s just
taking it to the back.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: You keep the old ones in the back, that is so ageist.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Well we have to make room for the fresh ones.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: So, what happens to the old guys?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Well, they go into the chipper.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Why, do I have a feeling that’s not as happy as it sounds? (Joey
points out one going into the chipper to her, as this haunty, demonic music starts to play
in the background) No! Nooooo!!! (she winces in horror and hides her face against
Joey’s shoulder, as she sees the tree spit out from the chipper.)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (to the guy operating the chipper) Hey! Hey!! (makes the ‘cut
it’ motion with his hands)
[Scene: Central Perk, all except Phoebe are there, Ross is telling the gang, minus
Rachel who’s still being retrained, about the different cookie options.]

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: ...and these come in the shapes of your favourite Christmas characters,
Santa, Rudolph, and Baby Jesus.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: All right, I’ll take a box of the cream filled Jesus’s.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Wait a minute, one box! Come on, I’m trying to send a little girl to
Spacecamp, I’m putting you down for five boxes. Chandler, what about you?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Ahh, do you have any coconut flavoured deities?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No, but ah, there’s coconut in the Hanukkah Menoreoes. I tell you
what, I’ll put you down for eight boxes, one for each night.
(Chandler mouths ‘Okay.’)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Mon?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: All right, I’ll take one box of the mint treasures, just one, and
that’s it. I-I started gaining weight after I joined the Brown Birds. (to Ross)
Remember, how Dad bought all my boxes and I ate them all?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah, no Mon, Dad had to buy everyone of your boxes because
you ate them all. But ah, y'know I’m sure that’s not gonna happen this time, why
don’t I put you down for three of the mint treasures and just a couple of the
Rudolph’s.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, come on, now you know you want ‘em.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Don’t, don’t, don’t, don’t, don’t do this.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I’ll tell you what Mon, I’ll give you the first box for free.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (she reaches out for it and stops) Oh God! I gotta go! (runs out)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Come on! All the cool kids are eating ‘em! (chases after her.)
[cut to Gunther retraining Rachel.]

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: And when you have a second later, I wanna show you why we don’t
just trap spiders under coffee mugs and leave them there.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (sitting down next to Chandler) I’m training to be better at a job
that I hate, my life officially sucks.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Look Rach, wasn’t this supposed to a temporary thing? I thought you
wanted to do fashion stuff?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Well, yeah! I’m still pursuing that.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: How... exactly are you pursuing that? Y'know other than sending out
resumes like what, two years ago?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Well, I’m also sending out.... good thoughts.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: If you ask me, as long as you got this job, you’ve got nothing
pushing you to get another one. You need the fear.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: The fear?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: He’s right, if you quit this job, you then have motivation to go
after a job you really want.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Well then how come you’re still at a job that you hate, I mean why
don’t you quit and get ‘the fear’?
(Chandler and Joey both laugh)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Because, I’m too afraid.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I don’t know, I mean I would give anything to work for a designer,
y'know, or a buyer.... Oh, I just don’t want to be 30 and still work here.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah, that’d be much worse than being 28, and still
working here.

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: Rachel?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: Remind me to review with you which pot is decaf and which is regular.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Can’t I just look at the handles on them?

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: You would think.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Okay, fine. Gunther, y'know what, I am a terrible waitress, do you know
why I’m a terrible waitress? Because, I don’t care. I don’t care. I
don’t care which pot is regular and which pot is decaf, I don’t care where the
tray spot is, I just don’t care, this is not what I want to do. So I don’t think
I should do it anymore. I’m gonna give you my weeks notice.

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: What?!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Gunther, I quit.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Joey) Does this mean we’re gonna have to start paying for
coffee? (Joey shrugs his shoulders.)
Commercial Break
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's, Chandler is entering numbers on a calculator as Ross reads
off how much he’s sold.]

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: ....and 12, 22, 18, four... (Chandler starts laughing) What?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I spelled out boobies.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (comes up and starts looking through Ross’s cookie supply) Ross,
but me down for another box of the mint treasures, okay. Where, where are the mint
treasures?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah, we’re out. I sold them all.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Monica, I’m cutting you off.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: No. No, just, just, just a couple more boxes. It-it-it’s no big
deal, all right, I’m-I’m cool. You gotta help me out with a couple more boxes!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Mon, look at yourself. You have cookie on your neck.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (covers her neck) Oh God! (runs to the bathroom)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: So, how many have you sold so far?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Check this out. Five hundred and seventeen boxes!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh my God, how did you do that?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Okay, the other night I was leaving the museum just as ‘Laser
Floyd’ was letting out of the planetarium, without even trying I sold 50 boxes!
That’s when it occurred to me, the key to my success, ‘the munchies.’ So I
ah, started hitting the NYU dorms around midnight. I am selling cookies by the case. They
call me: 'Cookie Dude!'

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (entering) Okay, stop what you’re doing, I need envelope stuffers,
I need stamp lickers.....

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well hey, who did these resumes for ya?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Me! On my computer.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well you sure used a large font.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Eh, yeah, well ah, waitress at a coffee shop and cheer squad
co-captain only took up so much room.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hey-hey-hey that’s funny! Your funny Chandler! Your a funny guy!
You wanna know what else is really funny?!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Something else I might have said?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I don’t know, I don’t know, weren’t you the guy that told
me to quit my job when I had absolutely nothing else to do. Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha!!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Sweetie, calm down, it’s gonna be okay.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: No, it’s not gonna be okay Ross, tomorrow is my last day, and I
don’t have a lead. Okay, y'know what, I’m just gonna, I’m just gonna call
Gunther and I’m gonna tell him, I’m not quitting.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: You-you-you don’t wanna give into the fear.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: You and your stupid fear. I hate your fear. I would like to take you and
your fear....

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (entering, interrupting Rachel) Hey! I got great news!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Run, Joey! Run for your life! (runs out)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: What? Rachel, listen, have you ever heard of Fortunata Fashions?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Well my old man is doing a plumbing job down there and he heard they have
an opening. So, you want me to see if I can get you an interview?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh my God! Yes, I would love that, oh, that is soo sweet, Joey.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Not a problem.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Thanks.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: And now for the great news.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What, that wasn’t the great news?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Only if you think it’s better than this... (holds up an aerosol can)
snow-in-a-can!! I got it at work. Mon, you want me to decorate the window, give it a kind
of Christmas lookie.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Christmas cookie?

scenes.location: Joey work, Joey is showing a guy a tree.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Okay, and ah, this one here is a Douglas Fir, now it’s a little more
money, but you get a nicer smell.

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: Looks good. I’ll take it.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (running up carrying a tree) Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait! No, no, you
don’t want that one. No, you can have this cool brown one. (points to the almost dead
tree she has)

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: It’s-it’s-it’s almost dead!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Okay but that’s why you have to buy it, so it can fulfil it’s
Christmas destiny, otherwise there gonna throw it into the chipper. Tell him, Joey

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Yeah, the ah, trees that don’t fulfil their Christmas destiny are
thrown in the chipper.

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: I-I think I’m gonna look around a little bit more.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Pheebs, you gotta stop this, I working on commission here.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (entering) Hey, guys. I’m here to pick out my Christmas tree.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well look no further, (shows her the dead one) this one’s yours!
Ahhh.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Is this the one that I threw out last year?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: All right y'know what, nevermind! Everyone wants to have a green one!
I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to get so emotional, I guess it’s
just the holidays, it’s hard.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh honey, is that ‘cause your Mom died around Christmas?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh, I wasn’t even thinking about that.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh. (turns and looks at Joey, who gives a ‘way-to-go’ thumbs
up and smile.)
[Scene: A Brown Bird meeting, Ross is there with the other Brown Birds to see who won
the contest.]

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to the girl sitting next to him) Hi there. How many, how many ah, did you
sell?

lines.speaker: Girl
lines.text: I’m not gonna tell you! You’re the bad man who broke
Sarah’s leg.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hey now! That was an accident, okay.

lines.speaker: Girl
lines.text: You’re a big scrud.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What’s a scrud?

lines.speaker: Girl
lines.text: Why don’t you look in the mirror, scrud.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I don’t have too. I can just look at you.

lines.speaker: Leader
lines.text: All right girls, and man. Let’s see your final tallies. (all the
girls raise their hands) Ohhhh, Debbie, (looks at her form) 321 boxes of cookies, (to
Debbie) Very nice.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to himself) Not nice enough.

lines.speaker: Leader
lines.text: Charla, 278. Sorry, dear, but still good.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to himself) Good for a scrud.

lines.speaker: Leader
lines.text: Oh, yes Elizabeth. Ah, 871.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: That’s crap!! Sister Brown Bird. (to Elizabeth) Good going. (does the
salute)

lines.speaker: Leader
lines.text: Who’s next? (goes over and stands behind Ross, who’s
feverishly writing on his form, and clears her throat to get his attention.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi there!

lines.speaker: Leader
lines.text: Hi. And batting for Sarah, Ross Geller, 872. Although, it looks like you
bought an awful lot of cookies yourself.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Um, that is because my doctor says that I have a very serious....
nuget.... diffency.

scenes.location: Central Perk, Chandler, Phoebe, and Ross are there.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Tell us what happened, Brown Bird Ross.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well, I lost. Some little girl loaned her uniform to her nineteen year old
sister, who went down to the U.S.S. Nimitz, and sold over 2,000 boxes.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Rachel, who’s entering) Hey! How’d the interview go?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, I blew it. I wouldn’t of even hired me.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, come here sweetie, listen, you’re gonna go on like a thousand
interviews before you get a job. (she glares at him) That’s not how that was supposed
to come out.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: This is the worst Christmas ever.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Y'know what Rach, maybe you should just, y'know stay here at the
coffee house.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I can’t! It’s too late! Terry already hired that girl over
there. (points to her) Look at her, she’s even got waitress experience. Last night
she was teaching everybody how to make napkin.... (starts to cry) swans.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: That word was swans.
[Scene: The hallway between the two apartments, Chandler, Phoebe, Ross, and Rachel are
coming up the stairs.]

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well seeing that drunk Santa wet himself, really perked up my
Christmas.
(They start to go into Monica and Rachel’s, their apartment is filled with all of
the old Christmas trees from Joey’s work.)

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh! Oh my God!

lines.speaker: Joey and Monica
lines.text: (jumping up from behind the couch) Merry Christmas!!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: You saved them! You guys! Oh God, you’re the best!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: It’s like ‘Night of the Living Dead Christmas Trees.’
(phone rings)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (answering the phone) Hello? (listens) Yeah, this is she. (listens) Oh!
You’re kidding! You’re kidding! (listens) Oh thank you! I love you!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Sure, everybody loves a kidder.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (hanging up the phone) I got the job!

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: That’s great! Hey! Excellent!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh, God bless us, everyone.

scenes.location: Central Perk, Rachel is serving her last cup of coffee.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Here we go. I’m serving my last cup of coffee. (the gang starts
humming the graduation theme) There you go. (hands it to Chandler) Enjoy. (they all cheer)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Ross) Should I tell her I ordered tea?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Um, excuse me, everyone. Ah, this is my last night working here, and I
ah, just wanted say that I made some really good friends working here, and ah, it’s
just time to move on. (at the counter Gunther starts to cry and runs into the back room)
Ah, and no offence to everybody who ah, still works here, you have no idea how good it
feels to say that as of this moment I will never have to make coffee again.

scenes.location: Rachel’s new job, Rachel’s boss is telling her what to do.

lines.text: Rachel’s Boss: Now Mr. Kaplan Sr. likes his coffee strong, so your gonna
use two bags instead of one, see. Now pay attention, ‘cause this part’s tricky,
see some people use filters just once.

title: The One Where Chandler Can't Remember Which Sister

lines.text: [Scene: Monica and Rachel's, Monica, Phoebe, Ross, Joey, and Rachel are
there, Joey is demonstrating a card trick.]

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Okay, pick a card, any card. (Monica picks one) All right, now memorize
it. Show to everybody. Got it?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Um-mm.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: All right, give it back to me. (takes the card back, but he looks at the
card before he puts it back in the deck, he holds the deck to his forehead, and thinks a
little while) 5 of hearts.
(Monica is sarcastically amazed.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Real magic does exist.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Wow. Joey, (sarcastically) how do you do it?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: I can’t tell you that, no.
(We hear some knocking coming from the ceiling.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah, somebody’s at the door on the ceiling.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Noo, that’s our unbelievably loud upstairs neighbor.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: He took up the carpet, and now you can hear everything.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Why don’t you go up there and ask him to ‘step lightly,
please?’

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I have like five times, but the guy is so charming, that I go up there
to yell and then I end up apologizing to him.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Ooh, that is silly. (gets up) I’ll go up there, I’ll tell him
to keep it down.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: All right, be my guest.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Good luck.
(Phoebe exits)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: All right, all right, all right, all right, all right, you really wanna
know how I did it, I’ll show ya. When you handed me back the card, what you
didn’t see was, I looked at it so fast that it was invisible to the naked eye. (picks
up a card and quickly looks at it) I just did it. (does it again) I just did it, again.
Here, I’ll slow it down so that you guys can see it. (looks and the card in slow
motion)

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Oh, I got it.
(We hear Phoebe knock at the door upstairs, and the guy answer it.)

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (muffled through the floor) Yeah, look I was with my friend downstairs
and we hear everything up here that you do, and I am sick and tired... (I tired but the
rest is unintelligible).

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: (muffled) Whoa, you are very beautiful.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (muffled) Oh, thank you.
Opening Credits

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's, continued from earlier.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (entering) Hey, anybody got a length of rope about six feet long with
a little nouse at the end?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Honey, what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I just saw Janice.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah, she was at Rockefeller Center skating with her husband, she
looked so happy. I almost feel bad for whipping that kid’s pretzel at them.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Man, I remember the first time I saw that girl Katherine, after we broke
up. She was just walking with her friend Donna, just laughing and talking. God, it killed
me.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yes, but you ended up having sex with both of them that afternoon.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Sorry, I just, any excuse to tell that story y'know....

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hey Chandler, there’s a party tomorrow, you’ll feel better then.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh, y'know what, I’m gonna be okay, you don’t have to throw
a party for me.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: It’s Joey’s birthday.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh, well then, if anybody should have a party it should be him.
(We hear Phoebe’s muffled voice through the ceiling.)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Sush!! I cannot believe she is still up there.
(We hear the guy telling a joke, and Phoebe laughing.)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Okay, well he totally screwed up the punch line. Y'know, it’s
supposed to be arrghh-eh og-errigh.

scenes.location: Fortunata Fashions, Rachel’s new job.

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: (entering) How’s that coffee comin,’ dear?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (jumping up from reading her magazine) Yeah, right away Mr. Kaplan.

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: I’m not supposed to drink coffee, it makes me gassy.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I know!

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: I’ll bet your thinking, ‘What’s an intelligent girl
who wants to be in fashion, doing making coffee?’ Eh?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Op.

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: Eh.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, you got me.

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: Well, don’t think I haven’t noticed your potential. Well,
I’ve got a project for you that’s a lot more related to fashion. How does that
sound?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, that sounds great.

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: Come on over here, sweetheart. (they walk over to a storage closet)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh thank you so much Mr. Kaplan, thank you so much.

lines.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
lines.text: (opening the closet door revealing that it’s full of tangled up
hangers.) I need these hangers separated ASAP. (she is stunned) You’re welcome.

scenes.location: The Moondance Diner, Rachel is talking to Monica about her job.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh God, I hate my job, I hate it, I hate my job, I hate it.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I know honey, I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, I wanna quit, but then I think I should stick it out, then I think
why would such a person stay in such a demeaning job, just because it’s remotely
related to the field they’re interested in.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (gives her a look) Gee, I don’t know Rach. Order up!! I got a
Yentel soup, a James Beans, and a Howdy hold the Dowdy!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh honey, come on, I’m sorry, I didn’t.... I don’t mind
paying my dues, y'know, its just how much am I gonna learn about fashion by walking Mira,
the arthritic seamstress, to the bathroom.
(A guy at the end of the table starts laughing.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (to him) Hi! Is my misery amusing to you?

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: I’m sorry, I wa, I wa, I was just ah.... (starts to laugh again)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: It’s not funny, this is actually my job.

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: Oh believe me, I-I-I’ve been there. I had to sort mannequin heads at
that Mannequins Plus.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh well then, so I’m just going to go back to talking to my friend
here. And you can go back to enjoying your little hamburger.

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: Ah, just one other thing.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yes?!

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.text: I ah, I work at Bloomingdale’s and I might know of a job
possibility if your, if your interested?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (looks at Monica) (to him) Do you want my pickle?

scenes.location: Chandler and Joey's, it’s Joey’s party.

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: (to Monica and Phoebe) Hey guys.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Hey Gunther. Hi. (to Phoebe) I mean you’re going out on a date with
the noisy guy upstairs?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well, he’s very charming.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I know, he’s too charming, but if you two start going out, then
it’s just gonna make it so much harder for me to hate him.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well, you’re just gonna have to try.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Joey, where are the Jell-o shots?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: I don’t know, Chandler is supposed to be passin’ ‘em
around...
(Camera cuts to show Chandler giving a Jello shot to the ceramic dog and holding an
empty tray of Jello shots.)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Chandler!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Hello-dillillio!!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, somebody’s feeling better.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (to Chandler) Stick out your tongue.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Monica) Take off your shirt!
(Chandler sticks out is tongue and it’s a horrible shade of green.)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh my!!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Oh my God! How many of these things did you have? These are pure vodka.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah, Jell-o just like Mom used to make.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (entering, to Ross) The most unbelievable thing happened to me today.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hi! So I’m out having lunch at Monica’s and this guy starts
talking to me, and it turns out he works for a buyer at Bloomingdale’s and
there happens to be an opening in his department. So I gave him my phone number and
he’s gonna call me this weekend to see if he can get me an interview!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Wow!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I know!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What, so this guy is helping you for no apparent reason?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Uh-huh!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: And he’s, he’s a total stranger?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah! His name is um, Mark something.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Huh. Sounds like Mark Something wants to have some sex.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: What!?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well, I’m just saying, I mean why else would he just, y'know, swoop
in out of nowhere for no reason.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: To be nice.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hey, Joey. Are men ever nice to strange women for no reason?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: No, only for sex.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Thank you. (to Rachel) So did you ah, did you tell Mark Something about
me?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I didn’t have to, because I was wearing my ‘I heart Ross’
sandwich board and ringing my bell.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Uh-huh.
Joey’s Sisters: (entering) Joey!!! Happy Birthday!! (all 7 of them look
almost identical)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Hey!! Hey-hey-hey!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Monica) Okay, how many of that girl are you seeing?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: How hammered are you? Huh? These, these are Joey’s sisters.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Hi Joey’s sisters!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (to one of his sisters, Cookie) Hey!

lines.speaker: Cookie
lines.text: Hey. What are we drinkin’ over here.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well, I have ah, vodka and cranberry juice.

lines.speaker: Cookie
lines.text: No kiddin,’ that’s the exact same drink I made myself right
after I shot my husband.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Wow. Okay, I don’t know how to talk to you.
(Cut to Chandler)
Sister 1: (to Chandler) What ‘cha doing?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh, I’m taking my ex-girlfriend of my speed dialer.
Joey’s Sisters: Oh!!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: No-no-no-no, no, it’s a good thing. Why must we dial so speedily
anyway? Why must we rush through life? Why can’t we savor the precious moments? (to
one of Joey’s sisters) Those are some huge breasts you have.
(Cut to Ross and Monica)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah. So um, I-I heard about this ah, Mark guy that ah, Rachel met today.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Isn’t that great?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh yeah! So ah, kinda pretty, pretty good. He sounds like a nice, good
guy.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh, he is. And he is so dreamy. I mean, y'know what, when he left I
actually used the phrase, ‘Hummina-hummina-hummina.’ (walks away)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: That’s excellent.

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's, Monica, Phoebe, Ross, and Rachel are eating breakfast.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to Rachel) So, he’s just a nice guy. You really think this Mark
doesn’t want anything in exchange for helping him?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Well, I assume I’ll have to take showers with him, but y'know,
that’s true of any job.
(Chandler enters hungover and groaning)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: How ya feelin’?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well, my apartment isn’t there anymore, because I drank it.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Where’d you get too? We lost you after you opened up all the
presents.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah, I ended up in the storage room, and not alone.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Woooo hoooo!!!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Ow, no ‘woo-hooing,’ no ‘woo-hooing.’

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Why, what happened?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Ah, I fooled around with Joey’s sister. (Phoebe gasps) Well,
that’s not the worst part.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What is the worse part?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I can’t remember which sister.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to Rachel) You see what men do! Don’t tell me men are not nice!
(points to Chandler) This is men!!
Commercial Break

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's, continued from earlier.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Are you insane? I mean Joey, is going to kill you, he’s actually
going to kill you dead.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Okay! You don’t think I thought of that?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: How can you not know which one?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I mean that’s unbelievable.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I mean, was it Gina?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Which one is Gina?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Dark, big hair, with the airplane earrings.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: No, no, no, that’s Dina.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Monica) You see you can’t tell which one is which either,
dwha!!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: We didn’t fool around with any of them. Dwha! Dwha!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Veronica. Look, it’s got to be Veronica, the girl in the red
skirt. I definitely stuck my tongue down her throat.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: That was me.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Look, when I’ve been drinking, sometimes I tend to get overly
friendly, and I’m sorry.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: That’s okay.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: That’s all right.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: That’s okay.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (angrily entering, to Chandler) Can I talk to you for a second?!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hey, Joey.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hey. (they all walk away from Chandler)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Come on!! (motions for Chandler to come with him)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Why can’t we talk in here? With, with, witnesses.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: I just got off the phone with my sister.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah, which, which one?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Mary-Angela.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Mary-Angela.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Y'know which one was she again?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Why don’t you ask Chandler, ‘cause he’s the one that fooled
around with her. She told me you said you could really fall for her. Now is that
true? Or are you just gettin’ over Janice by groping my sister.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: It’s gotta be the first one.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Really? That’s great! You and my sister, sittin’ in a tree.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yep, I’m in a tree.

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's, Monica is writing letters as Rachel enters.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Did he call? Did Mark call?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: No honey, I’m sorry, but the weekend’s not over yet.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh. (we hear laughing from the upstairs apartment) Oh my God, is that
Phoebe?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I guess they’re back from their date.
(He starts to play music.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Music. Very nice.
(We hear them start making out upstairs.)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh my God!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: So, how are you?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I am good. I finished my book.
(Things start to get really hot upstairs.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh yeah, what’s it about?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I don’t remember. Do you wanna take a walk?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah, I do. (they both run out)

scenes.location: Chandler and Joey's, Ross is reading a letter that Chandler wrote.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Dear Mary-Angela. Hi. How’s it going. This is the hardest letter
I’ve ever had to write. (to Chandler) What the hell’s a matter with you? How do
you think Joey’s going to react when he finds out that you blew off his sister with a
letter?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well, that’s the part where you tell him that I moved to France.
When actually I’ll be in Cuba.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: All right, look, look, you’ve got to do this yourself, okay in
person. At least you know her name. You just go to the house and you ask for Mary-Angela,
okay, when which ever one she is comes to the door, you take her for a walk, you let her
down easy.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: What if Mary-Angela comes to the door and I ask for Mary-Angela?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Where in Cuba?
[Scene: Joey’s sister’s house, Chandler hits himself on the head three times
and knocks on the door three times. Joey answers it.]

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (shocked) Joey, what-wh-wh-wha-wh-wha-wh-wha-wh-wha-what are you doing
here?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Waiting for my Grandma to finish my laundry. What about you?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I’m here to see Mary-Angela.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: You are so the man! (motions him to come in, and he does) Now look,
listen, listen, you got to be cool, ‘cause my Grandma doesn’t know about you two
yet, and you do not want to tick her off. She was like the sixth person to spit on
Mussolini's hanging body. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Where’s Mary-Angela?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: She’s right in there. (motions to the living room)
(Chandler walks into the living room, and sees all of Joey’s sisters, all wearing
red.)
Joey’s Sisters: Hey, Chandler!

scenes.location: Central Perk, Monica, Ross, and Rachel are there.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I can’t believe Mark didn’t call. It’s Sunday night, and
he didn’t call.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Bummer.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (to Ross) Yeah, right. Look at you, you’re practically giddy.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No, I’m genuinely sorry the Mark thing didn’t work out. Look,
Rach, I want only good things for you.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Wait a minute, why don’t you just call Mark. (they both look up in
shock) I mean, who says you have to sit here and wait for him, you’ve got to make
stuff happen.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: But, you, you don’t want to seem too pushy.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (to Ross) Honey, it’s not pushy, he gave her his home number.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to Rachel, as she gets his number) What, he gave you his home number? As
in like, to, to his home?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah, and you don’t mind if I call, because you only want good
things for me.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: That’s right good things, that-that is what I said. (glances at
Monica)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (on phone) Hello, Mark? Hi, it’s Rachel Green. (listens) Oh no,
don’t you apologize. (listens) Yeah, I’ll hold. (to Monica and Ross) He left my
number at work, but he was helping his niece with her report on the pioneers.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: That is so made up!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (on phone) Yeah, oh my God, tomorrow! That, no, it’s perfect. Oh
God, thank you soo much. Great! Bye! (hangs up phone) I got the interview!

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Yay!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: There you go.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: He even offered to meet me for lunch tomorrow to prep me for it.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh, that is amazing!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah well, if I know Mark, and I think I do, I’d expect nothing less.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I got to figure out what I’m going to wear.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: High collar and baggy pants say I’m a pro.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah! Right! Okay, I’ll see you guys later. (starts to leave) Woo
hoo!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: You go get ‘em. (to Monica) What did I do to you? Did I hurt you in
some way?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: ‘Why don’t you call him?!’ Well, thank you very much!
Y'know now he is going to prep her, y'know prep her, as in what you do when you surgically
remove the boyfriend!

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Are you crazy?!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Am I! Am I! Am I out of my mind! Am I losing my senses!! This dreamy guy
is taking my girlfriend out for a meal.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What?! Ross y'know this isn’t even about you! I mean this is about
Rachel and something wonderful happening for her. I mean you know even if you’re
right, what if he wants to sleep with her, does it mean he gets too?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I mean don’t you trust her?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well, yeah!

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Then get over yourself! Grow up!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (shyly) You grow up.

scenes.location: Joey’s sister’s house, they’re finishing up dinner.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: This teramisu is, is excellent. Did you make it Mary-Angela?
Joey’s Grandmother: No! I did!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well, it’s, it’s yummy. So Mary-Angela do you like it?
Joey’s Grandmother: Of course! It’s her favorite.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: So um, Mary-Angela, what’s your second favorite?
Joey’s Grandmother: More of Grandma’s teramisu.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Would you just please....give me the receipt ‘cause this is
great. It’s top notch.
Joey’s Grandmother: That dies with me.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: So will I.
Joey’s Sister: Excuse yourself, and go to the bathroom.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh no-no-no I was just squinting. That doesn’t mean anything.
Joey’s Sister: (whispering in his ear) Just do it.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Will you excuse me I have to um..... (walks to the hall)
[Cut to the hall, Joey’s sister runs up and grabs Chandler’s butt.]

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (startled) Hey!
Joey’s Sister: Finally, I thought we’d never be alone. Can I just tell
you something, I have not stopped thinking about you since the party. (kisses him)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Look, I may have jumped the gun here. (she tries to kiss him, but he
ducks it and moves away) Um, I just got out of a relationship and I’m not really in
a, in a commitment kind of place.
Joey’s Sister: So! Me neither! God, Mary-Angela was right you do have the
softest lips.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Ahhhh, you’re not Mary-Angela.
Joey’s Sister: No, I’m Mary-Theresa.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: This is so bad. If-if you’re not Mary-Angela, then-then who is?
Mary-Angela: (standing behind Chandler) I am!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh, this is soo bad. (doesn’t see Mary-Angela)
Mary-Angela: Joey!!!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: No Joey! No Joey! Don’t Joey! Joey!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: What’s goin’ on?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (pats him on the shoulder) You’re it! Now run and hide!
Mary-Theresa: It’s no big deal. Chandler was just kissin’ me because
he thought I was Mary-Angela.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: What?! How could you do that, how could you think she was Mary-Angela?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I wasn’t sure which one Mary-Angela was. (all of Joey’s
sisters gasp) Look, I’m sorry okay, I was really drunk, and you all look really
similar.
Joey’s Sister: I say, punch him Joey.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Yeah! Punch him!!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Y'know what, we should all calm down because your brother’s not
going to punch me. (to Joey) Are ya?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Well, that is usually what I would do. But I just never thought you’d
be on the receiving end of it. How could you do this?!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Joey if you wanna punch me, go ahead, I deserve it. But I just want
you to know that I would never soberly hurt you or your family, you’re my best
friend. I would never do anything like this ever again.

lines.speaker: Cookie
lines.text: So what. I say, punch him.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Yeah! Punch him! Punch him!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: No! No! No! No, I’m not going to punch Chandler.

lines.speaker: Cookie
lines.text: I’ll do it.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: No you won’t. Look he knows he did a terrible thing and I believe
him, he’s sorry. But, (to Chandler) you’ve got one more apology to make, all
right, you’ve got to apologize to Mary-Angela.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Okay, absolutely!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: You’ve got it. (he starts to look at his sister’s, but he
still doesn’t know which one is Mary-Angela.)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Cookie, now you can punch him!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: What?! (Cookie punches him)

scenes.location: A lobby, Ross is waiting for Rachel, after her interview.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (getting of the elevator and noticing Ross) Hey!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: What are you doing here?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah y'know, this building is on my paper route so I... (gives her a flower)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi. (kisses her)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: How’d did it go?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh well, the woman I interviewed with was pretty tough, but y'know thank
God Mark coached me, because once I started talking about the fall line, she got all happy
and wouldn’t shut up.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I’m so proud of you.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Me too!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Listen, I’m ah, I’m sorry I’ve been so crazy and jealous
and, it’s just that I like you a lot, so...

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Rachel?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah. (turns around) Hi Mark!

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Hi. I just talked to Joanna, and she loves you. You got it, you got the
job.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, I did!

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (to Ross) Oh my God!! (she turns around and hugs Mark, not Ross)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Congratu!! (sees her hug Mark) -lations-lations.

title: The One with All the Jealousy

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's, Rachel is getting ready for her first day.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (running in from her bedroom, wearing only a towel) Okay. Hey. Umm. Does
everybody hate these shoes?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh yeah, but don't worry. I don't think anybody's gonna focus on that
as long as your wearing that towel dress.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (to Ross) Tell him.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (to Chandler) It's her first day at this new job. Your not supposed to
start with her!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: All right, I suppose I can wait a day. Hey, what are you doing Friday?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I need you to come to this bachelor party for my weird cousin Albert,
y'know he's the botanist.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh God. Y'know, botanists are such geeks.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah. Is that a dinosaur tie?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hmm? Oh, yeah. (he makes a growling sound)

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (entering, with about 20 purses hanging around her neck) Morning. Rach,
I'm here with the purses!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Phoebe) It must take you forever to find your keys.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (running into the living room) Thank you, thank you, thank you, Pheebs.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Your welcome, oh please not the one with the turtles.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: No, no, no, no turtles scare me. I don't need that today.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Honey, just relax, it's gonna be fine. Hey, umm,. why don't I come down
there and I'll take you out to lunch?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh honey, thank you, but Mark's taking me out.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Mark is that ah, the same Mark that helped you get the job?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah, it's kinda like a 'good luck on your first day' sort of thing. (to
Phoebe) Is this actually a lunchbox?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Umm, no, it's a purse. And there's a thermos in it.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: (to Ross) Hey, so can you make it on Friday?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What? Oh yeah, yeah I think so. Why am I invited to this again?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well apparently Albert has no friends. He's very excited about the
bachelor party though. I think actually the only reason he's getting married is so he can
see a stripper.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: A stripper at a bachelor party, that is so clich�. Why don't you get a
magician?!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well, if the magician can open my beer with his but cheeks, then all
right.
Opening Credits

scenes.location: Chandler and Joey's, Ross and Chandler are entering, Joey is on the phone.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: She's having lunch with him. She's having lunch with him. And you should
of seen the hug she gave him when she got the job. And, and, and, (to Joey) he's really
good looking. (Joey gives an enthusiastic thumbs up) What am I gonna do?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Don't do anything. Keep it inside. Learn how to hide your feelings!
(pause) Don't cry outloud.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (hanging up the phone) Yes! Guess who's in an audition for a Broadway
musical?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I want to say you but, that seems like such an easy answer.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: It is me! It's a musical version of Tale of Two Cities. So I think
I'm gonna sing New York, New York, and ah, oh I left My Heart in San Francisco.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah Joey, I don't think you get to pick the cities.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Mr. Dickens gets to pick 'em.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Who?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: I'll get you the Cliff Notes.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: The what?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: The abridgment.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Oh, okay. (to Ross) The what?

scenes.location: Rachel's office, Mark is training Rachel.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: ...and the style number, and the invoice number, and the shipping date.
Good. Any questions so far?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yeah. What kind of discount do we get?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Twenty percent.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh!! I love this job! (her phone rings) Wow! My first call.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Here, let me. (answers phone) Rachel Green's line, how may I help you?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (on phone) Hi, is Rachel there?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: And who may I say is calling?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: This is Ross?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Ross of.....

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Of Ross and Rachel.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Oh hi. It's, it's Mark.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh hey, hey Mark.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Hey, hold on a second.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hi honey!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hi! What's ah, what's Mark doing answering your phone?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, he's just goofing around.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ohhhhh yeah, that's, that's funny. Why ah, why isn't he goofing around in
his own office?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh honey, this is his office too. I told you we're Joanna's two
assistants.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Why does Joanna need two assistants, how, how lazy is she?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh! Oh my God! What did I just do?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I think I just shipped 3,000 bras to personnel. Oh honey, I gotta go.
(to Mark) Mark, I need you!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Okay, bye-bye. (starts slamming the receiver down in anger.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Ow! Ross!!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, oh, I'm, I'm, I'm sorry sweetie, I was just trying to ah, I'm dialing
another number. (hangs up)
[Scene: The Moondance diner, Monica is cleaning up with one of the waiters, with her
back turned to him she removes her fake breasts and hides them under her wig.]

lines.speaker: Jeannine
lines.text: (to Monica) All right, I just got changed in thirty seconds so you can
be alone with him. You'd better go for it.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Please, I'm not going for anything.

lines.speaker: Jeannine
lines.text: Well, if you don't, I will.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Would you please go?

lines.speaker: Jeannine
lines.text: Night Mon. Night Julio.

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: (to Jeannine) Adios.
(Monica starts wiping down the stools, as Julio follows along behind her replacing the
napkin holders.)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Look Julio, someone left their book here.

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: Ah actually, that is mine.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh yeah, what are you reading?

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: Flowers of Evil, by Beaudalire. Have you read it?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Have I read it? (pause) No, are you enjoying it?

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: I thought I would, but the translation's no good.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Your a poet and don't know it. (she turns away and makes a face like 'I
can't believe I just said that.')

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: Actually I ah, I am a poet.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh, then you do know it. (pause) So um what kind of things do you write
about?

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: Things that move me. The, the shadow of a tree, a child laughing, or this
lip. (points to her lip)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Mine? (points to her lower lip) Right here?

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: I can write an epic poem about this lip. (grabs her lower lip)

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: How would that go? (they kiss) Well, it didn't rhyme, but I liked it.

scenes.location: Joey's audition.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (singing) You've got to pick a pocket or two. Boyyyyssss, (picks a
handkerchief from the pianist's pocket) you've got to pick a pocket or two..........

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Lovely, just lovely.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Really? Thanks.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Listen Joey, we definitely want to see you for the callback on
Saturday.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Excellent, I'll be there.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Okay, and listen don't forget to bring your jazz shoes for the dance
audition.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Ahhh! My ah, my agent said it wasn't a dancing part.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Joey, all the roles got to dance a little. But believe me with your
dance background it'll be a piece of cake.

scenes.location: Chandler and Joey's, Chandler is reading Joey's resume.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: ....three years of modern dance with Twila Tharp! Five years with the
American Ballet Theater?!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Hey, everybody lies on their resume, okay. I wasn't one of the Zoom Kids
either.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well, can you dance at all?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Yeah, I can dance, y'know. (starts to dance really, really, really badly)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh no, no, no, no.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (covering her mouth in shock) What, what is that?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Sure, it looks stupid now, there's no music playing.
(phone rings)

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: All right, I have to get that, but no-no. (answering phone) Hello?
(listens) (happily) Hi! Yeah listen, I'm, I'm in need of a stripper and I was told that
you do that. (listens) Let me ask you this, what, what do you do for the extra hundred?
(listens) So would I, would I have to provide the grapes?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (entering) Hi!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh, how was last night with Julio, senorita?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: It was soo amazing, he is so sexy, and smart, which makes him even
sexier. Oh gosh, I gotta so you this. Last night, we were fooling around and he stops to
write a poem.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Get out! I couldn't stop if a meteor hit me.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Okay, we have our stripper. A miss Crystal Chandelier.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Well sure, you name a kid that, what do you expect them to grow up to be?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Anyway um, when he left he forgot to take the poem with him. Now, I am
like totally dense about poetry, but I think it's pretty good all right. Check it out.
(hands them the poem)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (reading) The Empty Vase. Translucent beauty...

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: To yourself. (finishing) Hey-hey-hey, y'know what that's pretty good.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh good, I think so too. Pheebs?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh yeah.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh, I'm so glad you guys like it. Yay! All right I gotta go to work.
(tries to take the poem)

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Whoa, I'm not done.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: All right, just give it back to me when your done. See you guys.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Bye-bye.
(Monica leaves)

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh my God, oh my God! Poor Monica!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: What, what, what?!

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: What?! He was with her when he wrote this poem. Look, (reading) 'My
vessel so empty with nothing inside. Now that I've touched you, you seem emptier still.'
He thinks Monica is empty, she is the empty vase!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: You really think that is what he meant?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Oh, totally. Oh, God, oh, she seemed so happy too.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Done.

scenes.location: Rachel's office, her desk is covered with stuff Ross has sent her.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: (reaching through the flowers) Do you have the, the Ralph Lauren file?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, yeah, sure, it's umm... (she picks up this bug and it starts to play
the theme from Love Story)

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Wh-what's that?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: It's from Ross, it's a love bug.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Wow! Somebody wants people to know you have a boyfriend.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh no, no-no-no, that's not, not, not, what he is doing. He's just, he's
just really romantic.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: (to Rachel) Ah, excuse me, are you Rachel Green?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: (being joined by the rest of the barbershop quartet) One, two, three...

lines.speaker: Quartet
lines.text: (singing) Congratulations on your first week at your brand new job! It
won't be long before your the boss.

lines.speaker: The Bass Barber
lines.text: Omm-pah, omm-pah, omm-pah.

lines.speaker: Quartet
lines.text: (singing) And you know who will be there to support... you?! Your one
and only boyfriend...

lines.speaker: The Bass Barber
lines.text: It's nice to have a boyfriend.

lines.speaker: Quartet
lines.text: Your loyal loving boyfriend Ross..... Ross!
Commercial Break
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's, Ross and Rachel are entering the living room from her
bedroom.]

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I'm hurt! I'm actually hurt, that you would think that I would send you
any of those things out of any thing other than love. Hurt! Hurt!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: All right Ross!! I get it!!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I mean my God...

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: You're hurt!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: ...can't, can't a guy send a barbershop quartet to his girlfriend's office
anymorrrrre!!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh, please, Ross it was so obvious! It was like you were marking your
territory. I mean you might have well have just come in and peed all around my desk!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I would never do that!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Look, I know what's going on here, okay, Mark explained it all to me. He
said this is what you guys do.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah well if, if, if Mark said that, than Mark's an idiot.

scenes.location: Central Perk, Chandler, Ross, Joey are there.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Mark's a genius!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Why?! How?! How is he a genius?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Look, don't you see what's happening here. Instead of hitting on her
right away, he's becoming her confidant. Now he's gonna be the guy she goes too to
complain about you.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What am I going to do?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Well, why don't you send her a musical bug, op, no you already did
that. All right look, you're going to have to go there yourself now, okay, make a few
surprise visits.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I don't know you guys.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: All right fine, don't do anything, just sit here and talk to us,
meanwhile she is talking to him about you. And he's being Mr. Joe Sensitive, and she
starts thinking 'Maybe this is the guy for me, because he understands me.'

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: And before you know it, she's with him. And you'll be all, 'Ohh, man!' And
he'll be all, 'Yes!' And us, we'll be like, 'Wh-whoa, dude.' And pretty soon you'll be
like, (sadly) 'Hhiii,' and, and, and, 'I can't go, Rachel and Mark might be there.' And
we'll be like, 'Man get over it, it's been four years!!'

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: He paints quite a picture doesn't he?

scenes.location: Rachel's office.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: (walking up to Mark) Here's the Shelly Siegal stuff from December.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: (turning around) And wait, I've got something for you. (kisses her)

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Mark!!

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: It's okay, Rachel knows.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah, but even soo.
(Ross appears in the hallway just outside of Rachel's office.)

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I can't help it, I'm just, I'm just crazy about you.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Ohhh! That is soo sweet! (gets up to get herself a cup of coffee)
(Ross is eavesdropping in the hallway.)

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay, okay look, I know I'm being Mr. Inappropriate today, but it's just
so tough, I mean see you walking around and I just wanna touch you and hold you, come on
no one's around, just, just kiss me.
(They start to kiss, and Ross rushes into the office to break it up.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: All right that's, that's it!! Get off her!

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: What is going on?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What's going on?! (throws the love bug at him) That's what's going on!!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (now standing behind Ross) Ross!
(Ross finally looks at the woman kissing Mark.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I have been down in your store for twenty minutes trying to get a tie!
What do I have to do to get some service?! (turns to Rachel) Hi Rach. (He's puts his hand
on her shoulder and she knocks it away.)

scenes.location: Joey's dance audition, Joey is warming up.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Ah Joey. Joey Tribbiani. Listen Joey, I got a problem, I just got a
call from my dance captain, he's having a relationship crisis and can't get out of Long
Island.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: So, does that mean the audition is off?

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Listen Joey, seeing as you've got the most experience, I want you to
take these dancers and show them the combination.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: What?!

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Aw come on Joey, it's easy. Y'know, it's hand, hand, head, head, (very
quickly, Joey watches stunned) up, pas de bouree, pas de bouree, big turn here, grand
sissone, sissone, sissone, slide back, step, step, step, and jazz hands!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: It's ah, step-ity, step and jazz hands.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Have fun.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: Bye. (does the jazz hands)

scenes.location: Monica and Rachel's, Monica is tying a ribbon to a vase.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (entering) Hey!

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: What are you wrapping?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh-ho, look what I got Julio.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Yeah, it's a vase.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Yeah, just like the one in the poem.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Well not exactly like the one in the poem.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What do you mean?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: Remember how you said you were really dense about poetry? Oh. (hugs her)

scenes.location: The Moondance Diner.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (to Julio) So! I'm just an empty vase, huh?

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Y'know, so I don't read as many important books as you do, and I don't
write trick poems that seem to be about one thing but are actually about something else.
And y'know what, I get excited about stupid stuff, like when I my People magazine
comes on Saturday, and the new Hold Everything catalog. Y'know but that does not
mean that I'm empty, I care about things. I care about my friends and family. You have no
right to make that kind of judgment about me.

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: You don't even know me...

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, the poem is not about you.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: The Empty Vase is not about you. My baby, you make me so sad that you
would think this.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: I'm sorry, my friend Phoebe...

lines.speaker: Julio
lines.text: No, it's about all women. Well, all American women. You feel better now?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (sarcastically) Oh yeah.

scenes.location: Joey's audition, the director has returned and wants to see the combination.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: All right, let's do it!
(The group does the same horrible dance that Joey did earlier in the show, except
they're all out of sync and they do the jazz hands at the end.)

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: No, no, no. What was that?

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: I know, it was the best I could get out of them.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Well, people!

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: People, people, people.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Let's try it again, and this time let's watch everybody watch Joey.
(to Joey) Show 'em how it's done. (to the pianist) Count it off.
(The pianist starts to play, and Joey readies himself, and then runs out of the
audition.)

scenes.location: Central Perk, Chandler and Rachel are there.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: So ah, did you have fun at the bachelor party last night?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh yeah, yeah! Look what I got, look what I got. (holds up a pen) See,
she's fully dressed, right?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: And then you click it and, uh-oh, she's naked. And then, and then you
click it again and she's dressed. She's a business woman, she's walking down the street,
she's window shopping, and (clicks pen) whoa-whoa-whoa, sh-she's naked! (Rachel just
stares at him.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (entering) Hi.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Y'know what, I'm, I'm gonna spend some alone time with the pen.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: (sits down next to her) I'm sorry, I was an idiot.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: A big idiot.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: A big idiot. Just you have to realize is, this whole Mark thing is kinda
hard for me.
(Gunther is eavesdropping in the background.)

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Honey, why is it hard, I mean we've been together for almost a year now?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Well, I was with Carol for like eight years and I lost her. And now if
it's possible I think I love you even more. So, it's hard for me to believe that I'm not
gonna, well that someone else is not going to take you away.

lines.speaker: Gunther
lines.text: Let it be me! Let it be me!

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Honey, that's very sweet, it just seems to me though, that if two people
love each other and trust each other, like we do, there's no reason to be jealous. (she
kisses him)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: I gotta get going. Bye Chandler.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Oh, okay Ross. Listen, this pen is kinda getting boring, so can you
pick me up some porn?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Where ya going?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, I've got to go pick up Ben, we've got a play date this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Ohh, with who?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh, just this woman that I met last night at the party.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: There was a woman at the... (realizes) The stripper?!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: You have a play date with a stripper?!

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Man, I gotta get a kid. (looks at the pen and starts laughing)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ah, yeah, yeah. Umm, we started talking after she y'know, did her thing.
And it turns out she's got a boy about Ben's age, so we're taking them to a gym-boree
class. Why, is that okay?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Sure, is she married?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Ahh, no.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh. (starts shaking the sugar down in a packet really hard.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Are you jealous?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Noo, I y'know I don't see why she has to play with you, that's all. I
mean doesn't she have any y'know other stripper moms friends of her own?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: You are totally jealous.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I'm not jealous. All right this is about, umm, people feeling certain
things y'know about strippers. And y'know, and um, I...

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Honey, I love you too.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Ugh. Wait, wait, wait.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What?
(She runs over and gives him a very passionate kiss.)

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Huh.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (to Chandler) Well, there's a kiss that he won't forget for a couple of
hours, y'know.

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah. Either that, or you just turned him on and sent him off to a
stripper.

title: The One Where Monica and Richard Are Just Friends

scenes.location: A Video Store, Monica is running in to return a video.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (to clerk) Hi.
(The clerk enters the video into the computer.)

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Six dollars, please.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Six? I just had it for one night. It’s three.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Eight o’clock is the cut-off and, (looks at his watch) aww,

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Y'know in a weird way, you have too much power. Look, you’re gonna
have to help me out here, ‘cause I only have three.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: (standing behind her, without his moustache) I can help with that.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh my God. Richard? (turns around) Hi!

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: Hi!

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Wow! Your lip went bald. (Richard pays the clerk) Hey, thanks.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: So, you look great.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: No you do. You... just...

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: You’ve got panties stuck to your leg.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: (removes them) That’s because I-I was just grabbing some things out
of the dryer, and it’s static cling. Or maybe it’s just that God knew I’d
be running into you and saw an opportunity.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: It’s good to see you.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: It’s good to see you too.
(They hug, and Richard notices a stocking stuck to Monica’s back, which he removes
for her.)
Opening Credits

scenes.location: continued from earlier.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: You see that guy? He’s in classics now, but y'know as soon as we
leave he’s going straight to the porn.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: He’s gonna go up to the counter with Citizen Kane, Vertigo,
and Clockwork Orgy. (they both laugh) This is nice.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: I missed this.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Me too.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: So, you wanna get a hamburger or something?

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: Oh, um, I don’t know if that’s a good idea.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: Oh. Look, just friends, I won’t grope you. I promise.

lines.speaker: Monica
lines.text: No, I just I think that it’s too soon.

lines.speaker: Richard
lines.text: No it’s not too soon, I had lunch at a eleven.
[Scene: Monica and Rachel's, Chandler, Ross. Joey, and Rachel are eating breakfast.
Chandler is holding a bottle of Hersey’s Syrup.]

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Yeah, baby!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: What are you doing?

lines.speaker: Chandler
lines.text: Making chocolate milk. Do you want some?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: No thanks. I’m 29.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: (looking at her watch) Oh my God, I gotta go to work!

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh sweetie, when do you think you’re going to get off tonight?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh I don’t know honey. It’s gonna be really late.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Oh come on, not again.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I know. I’m sorry. Look, I’ll make a deal with you all right?
Okay?

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: For every night that you’re asleep before I get home from work...

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: I will wake you up in a way that’s proved very popular in the past.

lines.speaker: Ross
lines.text: Now, if you need to stay late, I want to be supportive of that.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Phoebe
lines.text: (entering, holding a pair of Roller Blades) Hi.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Joey
lines.text: (to Phoebe) Look at you. Since when do you roller blade?

lines.speaker: Phoebe
